Summary

In 1693 Agatha Harkness who was always told she should have never been born met, and fell in love, with Death Herself, in 1750 she gave birth to twins Nicholas and Prudence, one strong, one sick, with her wife by her side. In 1760, after ten incredible years as a family of four, Rio and Agatha having no idea that their daughter was giving her magic and life force to her brother to keep him alive, Agatha woke to find both her children gone, but not with their other mother. After a devastating fight Agatha and Rio realise neither of them know where their children are, but what they do know is that all that matters is getting them back; not realising, that even working side by side, it will be centuries, for them, before they are reunited with their children. This is their story; Death and her Purple Witch.

    Chapter 1 AN: So, ever since I watched the final, I have thought of so many ideas of stories I wanted to write to give Agathario what they deserve. This story is going to combine a lot of the ideas I have together, it will likely be a very long story, even longer than Love Preserving. Everything should make sense as the story goes on, but I will add notes if needed. Hope you like this story and give it the support you have given my other Agathario fics. I intend to have this story go through all of Agatha and Rio’s history, while also having different storylines. There will be things that stick to the little we know from Cannon, and I am choosing to use some of the things Jac’s said in the post final interview as inspiration, but there will also be changes. Hope you enjoy.

    So, I really wanted you to read this story, so I am posting this chapter now, but the next chapter will not be posted until Tuesday as I actually have to go into the office tomorrow, after that I hope to update fairly regularly, at first it won’t be as regular as Love Persevering but I hope to eventually be able to update that often.

    March 17th 1693: Salem As long as she can remember Agatha Harkness has listened to her mother call her evil, say that she should never have been born, and she always refused to believe it, she wanted to believe she was good, but as she stares at the body of not just her mother, but her mother’s entire coven, who she just killed, Agatha can’t help but fear that her mother was right and that there is no good in her.

    “I’m going to prove you wrong,” Agatha says as she reaches down and takes a locket, a family heirloom, from her mother’s body. “I can be good,” Agatha says, her voice sounding determined, almost like the desire to prove that is going to keep her going.

    “Well, that is going to be interesting to see,” A voice says, and Agatha turns to see an incredibly beautiful woman wearing a green cloak, over a green dress, walking towards her.

    “Who are you? What do you want?” Agatha asks, causing her purple magick to appear in her hand, clearly ready to defend herself if needed, as in her experience people only hurt you.

    “You don’t have to fight me,” the woman says, walking towards Agatha, looking completely unphased by both the magick Agatha has in her hand, and the bodies that are covering the clearing.

    “Who are you?” Agatha asks, repeating the question, clearly not going to ‘disarm’ so to sense until her question is answered.

    “Rio,” She answers. “You can call me Rio,” Rio says, as she gets to right in front of Agatha. “My lady,” Rio says, presenting Agatha with a flower that she clearly created from nowhere.

    “You are a green witch,” Agatha says, staring at the woman and as she cannot see any malice in her eyes, something Agatha has gotten very good at telling due to necessity, Agatha reaches out and takes the flower from Rio.

    “You could say that,” Rio tells Agatha, smiling as she is glad that Agatha took the flower. “I heard the commotion, I thought I would come and see what was going on,”

    “You are late, you missed the show,” Agatha tells Rio, still trying to figure out what she meant by ‘you could say that,’.

    “No, I arrived right on time,” Rio tells Agatha with a smirk. “You are very impressive Agatha Harkness,” Rio tells Agatha, who is very confused about how this mystery woman knows who she is.

    “How do you know my name?” Agatha asks confused.

    “I know everything,” Rio admits, Agatha having no idea just how true that is. “Maybe one day I will tell you why,” Rio says, sounding completely fascinated by Agatha.

    “Do not strain yourself,” Agatha says, before she can think better of it, causing Rio to laugh. “What… what do you want from me?” Agatha asks nervously, as something tells her that there is something incredible about the woman, something that she can’t help but feel fascinated about. “Nothing… I just wanted to meet you,” Rio tells Agatha, as she has been watching from a far for a while, feeling draw to the younger witch, and after watching what Agatha just did, understanding the implications of it, she suspects she knows why that is. “You have survived Agatha Harkness, in ways few others have,” Rio tells Agatha, looking her up and down, clearly liking what she sees. “That makes you formidable, incredible,” Rio tells Agatha, Rio being the only being in the world who truly appreciates that.

    “I do not feel incredible,” Agatha admits, having no idea why she is actually admitting that to this woman she has never met before.

    “You will,” Rio says, giving Agatha such a charming smile that makes her feel like anything is possible. “Te Veo, Agatha Harkness,” Rio says, before walking away from Agatha, heading back into the trees she came out from. As Rio walks away Agatha watches her go, not being able to tear her eyes away from the incredible person, Agatha knowing that she has never met anyone like the incredible woman who just graced her presence. “Who was that, Women?” Agatha mutters, staring at the trees Rio disappear into, with an amazed look on her face, and once it becomes clear that Rio isn’t coming back Agatha pins her mothers broach to her shirt, and keeping the flower in her hand, uses her magick to fly away from her mother and coven; leaving the bodies scattered in the clearing; leaving Salem with no intention of ever returning.

    May 1693 Two months have passed since Agatha Harkness’s life has changed forever, since she killed her mother, and her coven, since she met a magnetic woman who Agatha has found herself unable to stop thinking about. It’s late afternoon and having just got into a fight, that was more physical than the magical ones Agatha is more comfortable with, Agatha is squatting at the banks of a river cleaning her bloodied hand, trying to see how bad the injury she has sustained is.

    “That looks painful,” A very familiar voice says, and Agatha turns to see Rio, wearing the same outfit she was wearing last time they saw each other, walking towards her, once again walking out of the trees. “Rio,” Agatha says, trying to make it seem like she isn’t completely amazed to see her.

    “You remember me,” Rio says, sounding almost glad about that. “You were hard to forget,” Agatha admits, as Rio gets to her side, Agatha not noticing that Rio looks rather proud that Agatha remembers her. “Good to know,” Rio admits, as she squats down next to Agatha. “What happened?” Rio asks, looking at the wound on Agatha’s hand. “I thought you said you knew everything,” Agatha comments, her guards up, remembering what Rio said last time and Rio laughs.

    “Humour me,” Rio responds, as she wants to know what Agatha is going to say about how she was hurt.

    “I miscalculated how protective people can be of their crops,” Agatha admits, and while Rio knows that is the truth, she also knows it’s not the full truth.

    “Why did you not use your magick?” Rio asks, wanting to know what Agatha is going to say to that, and Agatha looks down at the ground, clearly not wanting to talk about it. “Agatha?” Rio asks, in a gentle voice, speaking with Agatha with the kind of gentleness she has never heard someone use toward her before.

    “I am not using my magick anymore,” Agatha reveals, as she avoids looking at Rio.

    “Why not?” Rio asks curious, gently encouraging Agatha to talk more. “Because I want to be good,” Agatha admits, as she continues to be good. “Agatha your magic does not make you bad,” Rio says, and Agatha looks at her. “It is apart of you, something you cannot change,” Rio told Agatha, knowing that if someone as powerful as Agatha were to try to deny their magick it would be catastrophic for them, and in Agatha’s case there would be other devastating consequences that Rio doesn’t want to think about. “So, I cannot be good,” Agatha says, causing the realisation that her mother was always right to set in.

    “You already are,” Rio tells Agatha, who has no idea what to say about that because no one has ever shown her that kind of kindness. “May I see your hand?” Rio asks.

    “Why?” Agatha asks suspiciously.

    “Because I would like to help you,” Rio responds simply, not at all surprised that Rio is on edge, and clearly interested in what Rio is going to do Agatha offers her hand. Taking Agatha’s hand Rio brings it up to her mouth, gently blows on it, then brings it closer, and licks the blood off, healing the wound as she does. “There, much better,” Rio says, letting go of Agatha’s hand, Agatha feeling very much like she didn’t want Rio to let go. “How… how did you do that?” Agatha asks, looking between her hand, and Rio, with an amazed look on her face, as she has never heard of someone who was able to do that, not even a green witch.

    “Magick,” Rio answers, and Agatha gives her an annoyed look. “I gathered that,” Agatha responds, resisting the urge to roll her eyes. “I have never seen magick like this,” Agatha admits.

    “Because no one else has magick like me,” Rio admits. “Just like no one has magick like you Agatha,” Rio tells her. “Do not push it down, do not let others fear control you,” Rio says, knowing that is very important for Agatha’s sake.

    “Why are you so kind to me?” Agatha asks, as she has never experienced the kind of kindness Rio has shown her in their short meetings. “Because you deserve kindness,” Rio says, before standing up. “Te Veo,” Rio says, before stating to walk away.

    “Wait,” Agatha says, and Rio turns back around. “When will I see you again?” Agatha asks curious, not even realising that she phased the question as a when, and not an if.

    “Soon,” Rio says before once again disappearing into the trees. After watching Rio walks away Agatha turns back to the river to clean the rest of her blood, feeling fascinated by who Rio is and knowing that she is going to figure her out, hopefully, before she sees her again. September 1693 Four months have passed since Agatha las saw Rio, six months since she first met her, and despite only having two short conversations with her Agatha has found herself longing for the mysterious women. Since her second meeting with Rio Agatha has been thinking about her a lot, almost constantly, and those thoughts have led to Agatha developing a theory about just who Rio really is. For weeks Agatha has been looking for an opportunity to find out if her theory is correct, and as she stands near the body of a witch who had become a witch hunter and tried to add Agatha to her list of victims Agatha knows that this is the opportunity she has been waiting for.

    “Are you there?” Agatha asks, looking around, searching for a familiar flash of green. “If what I suspect is right you should be,” Agatha admits. “I see you figured me out,” Rio’s voice says, as she steps out of shadows, but this time unlike the green dress and cloak Agatha has become familiar with she is wearing a similar outfit in black. “Not many do,” Rio admits. “Do you reveal yourself to people often?” Agatha asks, not feeling afraid despite the fact that she knows exactly who Rio actually is. “No,” Rio says, walking closer to Agatha, noticing Agatha’s reaction, more specifically, noticing that Agatha doesn’t seem to be afraid of her, something which is very unusual for Rio as usually when people meet her they are afraid of her.

    “So, I am special,” Agatha realises, trying to make sense of everything going on.

    “In many, many ways,” Rio says, as she gets to Agatha. “Are you afraid?” Rio asks, watching Agatha carefully, with an intensity behind her eyes Agatha has never felt, as she tries to figure out just what is going on. “No,” Agatha responds as she obviously swallows. “Not of you,” Agatha admits.

    “Then tell me, Agatha, what are you afraid off?” Rio asks curious, moving a step closer to Agatha, so that she is standing even closer to Agatha, there being basically no space between the two of you.

    “What you make me feel,” Agatha admits, her voice quiet, but because Rio is so close she is able to hear her.

    “And what, may I ask, is that?” Rio asks, and for a moment Agatha debates the best way to answer that question, but as she decides that no words will accurately portray what she is feeling Agatha reaches out, grabs hold of Rio’s dress, and pulls her in for a kiss.

    For a second it is clear that Rio did not expect that, and doesn’t know what to do, something which makes Agatha terrified that she just made a huge mistake, but then just as she tries to pull back Rio deepens the kiss, pulling Agatha in close, as their tongues battle for dominance.

    “Does that answer your question?” Agatha asks one the two of them break apart, and Agatha has to try to catch her breath.

    “One of them,” Rio says, before pulling Agatha into another hurried kiss, Rio knowing, without a doubt, that what Agatha is making her feel is something she has never felt before, something she will do anything to hold onto.

    December 1693 Three months have passed since Agatha kissed death, something that didn’t make her die, but made her feel alive for the first time in her life. Since their first night together Agatha and Rio have continued to see each other when they can make it work, something which can be rather difficult when Rio is a cosmic being.

    It’s late at night, the last night of year, and Rio and Agatha are both lying on the banks of a river together, Agatha laying on Rio’s chest as Rio has her arms around Agatha, holding her close.

    “What does it feel like?” Agatha asks Rio, breaking the comfortable silence they have been lying in.

    “What does what feel like?” Rio asks, as she absentmindedly plays with Agatha’s hair, knowing that there are a lot of questions that that could lead to.

    “Being such a fundamental part of the universe,” Agatha responds. “I’m not really sure how to answer that,” Rio admits. “It’s just… what I’ve always known,” Rio admits. “It’s like I feel everything… but in someways nothing… except when I’m with you,” Rio admits, and Agatha is amazed by that.

    “I… wow,” Agatha says, having no idea how to respond to that. “So, I guess the end of the year does not really mean much to you,” Agatha assumes, changing the subject a little as she doesn’t know how to handle such a cosmic being so interested in her.

    “No, it does no,” Rio admits. “But I have spent enough time watching humanity to realise that symbols are important,” Rio admits. “And, from your perspective, what does the end of year symbolise?” Agatha asks curious.

    “Letting go,” Rio admits. “To me the end of the year is about letting go of the past, moving forward without the weight of what has been, to make the decision to let go of the shackles that binds; allowing oneself to start fresh by doing something that has been frightening before,” Rio explains, and for a few moments Agatha looks like she is pondering Rio’s words. “Interesting,” Agatha says, getting an idea, so she places a kiss on Rio’s cheek before standing up.

    “What are you doing?” Rio asks confused.

    “There is something I have always wanted to do but I was always too scared of mother,” Agatha admits, undoing her cloak and dropping it to the ground. “I want to swim naked in the moonlight as the year starts anew,” Agatha tells Rio, as the ladder pushes herself up, so she is sitting up. “Agatha, it’s freezing,” Rio reminds her.

    “And? I know you will keep me warm,” Agatha responds, as she starts to remove her clothing.

    “What makes you think I am joining you?” Rio asks.

    “Because I’m saying please,” Agatha responds. “Please, Sweetheart,” Agatha says, as she lets the last of her clothing fall to the ground. “Oh Agatha Harkness, the control you have over me,” Rio says, standing up and also letting her clothing fall to the ground.

    Once Agatha and Rio are both standing naked in the moonlight Agatha takes Rio’s hand and the two of them head to the river where they proceed to swim and kiss in the moonlight until, even with Rio’s powers, it becomes too cold, and they are forced to return to the bank where they enter the new year clinging to one another.

    January 1695 A little over a year has passed since Rio and Agatha started the new year together, and for the year that followed they have done their best to spend as much time together as possible, something which can be difficult when Rio has to do her job, but despite that they have been managing to see each other pretty regularly.

    It’s a winters day and as she needed to get out of the cold Agatha is in a table at the sole Tavern in a village in a town she has wondered into, reading a book, trying to keep away from everyone as she doesn’t want to deal with anyone. As Agatha reads, she realises as soon as someone has sat down across from her.

    “I would like to be alone,” Agatha says, without looking up from her book, as it is not the first time someone has tried to bother her. “That’s a pity,” A very familiar voice says, and Agatha looks up to see Rio, and as soon as she sees her, her face breaks out in a smile. “Rio,” Agatha says with a smile.

    “Now, that’s a much better reaction,” Rio admits, returning Agatha’s smile with her own “Do I warrant closing your book?” Rio asks curious, as she has learnt that Agatha closing a book is big deal.

    “This time,” Agatha says, closing her book.

    “Have you eaten?” Rio asks curious.

    “Had to to sit down,” Agatha admits. “Are you here to do your job?” Agatha asks, wanting to know what to expect, wanting to get some idea of how long Rio will be around for.

    “No, only play,” Rio admits, smirking at Agatha.

    “Well, in that case, how about we get a room upstairs,” Agatha suggests, as she was planning on moving on quickly, but considering Rio has joined her she isn’t apposed to sticking around.

    “I like the sound of that,” Rio said, and the two of them exchange smiles, and without another word the two of them slide out of the booth they are in.

    A few minutes after Rio surprised Agatha in the Taven the two of them are walking into the room they were able to rent and as soon as they walk into the room, the moment the door is closed, Agatha grabs hold of Rio and pushes her up against the wall and starts to kiss her.

    “Agatha.” Rio says, moaning as Agatha starts to kiss and suck on her neck, reaching behind her to lock the door. “Agatha…. I have something for you,” Rio reveals, wanting to give her gift before getting too caught up in what they are about to do, and once she does Agatha pulls back so she can look at her.

    “You do?” Agatha asks looking at Rio in surprise.

    “It is your birthday,” Rio reminds Agatha.

    “I did not think you knew that,” Agatha tells her, as it’s not something she talks about considering how her mother would react to her birthday, and as she does Rio reaches out and pushes Agatha’s hair out of her face. “Oh Honey, when are you going to learn, I know everything,” Rio reminds Agatha, as she reaches into her cloak and pulls out a small book and a flower. “Happy Birthday, Sweetheart,” Rio says, as she hands the two objects over to Agatha.

    “Thank you,” Agatha says, as she takes the book and flower, first she smells the flower and then she opens the book she realises that it is an empty journal, made of beautiful paper, as she flicks though Agatha realises that there is a message on the cover page; Agatha, I want you to fill this with all your beautiful thoughts, all your incredible spells, all the things you are afraid to share. Make this be a place that is truly yours; Yours, Rio “This is incredible,” Agatha says, as she runs her hands over the leather cover, realising there are small flowers etched into the leather. “No one has ever given me something this incredible, this carefully made,” Agatha admits, having no idea how to react to such a thoughtful gift. “You deserve it,” Rio tells Agatha, as in her opinion Agatha deserves everything. “You deserve beauty and kindness, and all the things you were deprived of,” Rio tells Agatha, as now that she has gotten to know Agatha better, she can’t help but feel like there is nothing she wouldn’t do to save her from more pain.

    “I….. I love you,” Agatha tells Rio, saying the words for the first time. “I didn’t think I was capable of that, but you have made me believe I can be…. I love you, Rio,” Agatha tells her, knowing she has never felt as scared to say three words as she just said.

    “I love you, Agatha Harkness,” Rio says before kissing Agatha, knowing, without a doubt, that when she is with Agatha, she feels more herself than she has felt in the eternity she has lived, she truly feels alive. As Agatha and Rio kiss Agatha gently puts down what she is holding down on a nearby table, and once she has put the precious objects down Agatha once again takes control of death in a way only, she can, and pushes her against the wall, her hand finding it’s way under Rio’s dress as they proceed to show each other exactly how they both feel.

    June 1695 Six months have passed since Agatha told Rio she loved her for the first time, since Agatha said those words to anyone for the first time, and over time Agatha has become more comfortable with telling Rio just what she feels for her.

    Due to being Death Rio is never surprised when she finds multiple bodies together, nor is she surprised when she sees signs that tell her Agatha is responsible for the bodies, but what is surprising is what said purple witch isn’t waiting for Rio with the bodies she created, as ever since Agatha figured out who she really is she would wait with any body she created for Rio to appear.

    Having a bad feeling Rio helps the souls of several adults, and a little girl, onto the Afterlife before returning to the physical realm. As soon as she returns to the physical Rio starts her search for Agatha, and without too much trouble, as all she has to do is follow her heart to find Agatha, she manages to find her.

    The instant Rio sees Agatha sitting alone in a forest Rio knows there is something horribly wrong, before she ever realises what she is doing Rio runs towards Agatha; having a feeling deep inside that tells her every second counts.

    “Agatha? Agatha, My love?” Rio asks, throwing herself onto the ground next to Agatha and seeing her loves arms covered in cuts, a consequence of being who she is that tells Rio she knows exactly what caused them. “Agatha? Agatha? Can you hear me?” Rio asks, trying to get Agatha to look at her as she tries to use all her abilities to figure out how hurt Agatha is, how much blood she has lost.

    “Ri…I tried to help her,” Agatha admits, clearly becoming weaker with every word. “I really tried,” Agatha admits, her blue eyes flickering open and close.

    “The little girl?” Rio asks, trying to put the pieces together, tyring to figure out exactly what happened, and Agatha nods. “I’m sure you did what you could,” Rio says, having no idea what happened, but knowing that it doesn’t matter right now, all that matters is looking after Agatha, keeping her alive, and once Rio is sure that she is, doing what needs to be done to help her be okay.

    “Was not enough, never enough,” Agatha says, and because of who she is Rio can tell Agatha starting to slip away from her.

    “No, no, no,” Rio says horrified, as she brings Agatha’s wrist towards her mouth.

    “Let me go… Rio… let me go,” Agatha pleads, as Rio desperately hopes that what she is about to do will work.

    “Never,” Rio says, and going against everything she is, Rio starts to use her healing abilities to heal Agatha’s self-inflicted injuries. It takes several minutes, minutes that for Rio feel like they are never going to end, but Rio manages to heal all the injuries Agatha inflicted on herself while Agatha herself looses consciousness.

    “Let’s get you somewhere safe,” Rio says, before taking Agatha into her arms and picking her up, and after checking to make sure nothing was left behind Rio carries Agatha through forest. With every step she takes Rio looks down at Agatha and reassures herself that the women she loves, the one person in the universe she knows she cannot loose, is still with her. A few hours after Rio found Agatha in the forest Agatha is still unconscious, lying on the bed of empty house Rio broke into, while Rio herself is sitting next to Agatha, ignoring everything but the feelings that is telling her that Agatha is alive.

    “What happened, My love?” Rio asks quietly. “Why did you think this was the answer?” Rio asks, as while she has a few suspicious about what could have happened, she has no idea if what she is thinking is right. For a little while Rio continues to watch Agatha, continues to watch her sleep, until she finally sees movement that tells her Agatha is starting to wake up.

    “Agatha? Agatha? Can you hear me?” Rio asks, moving closer to her love, and seconds after she does Agatha’s eyes open.

    “Rio?” Agatha asks. “Am I…” Agatha starts to say, then she realises. “You saved me,” Agatha realises, sounding almost disappointed. “I did,” Rio tells her.

    “I did not want to be saved,” Agatha says, an edge to her voice. “I thought that was obvious,” Agatha admits.

    “It was, I did not care,” Rio tells Agatha, the conformation that Agatha was actually trying to kill herself hurting Rio more than she thought was possible.

    “I thought you could not intervene,” Agatha says, as that’s what she assumed, that’s why she assumed that what she did would have worked. “I made an exception,” Rio responds, trying to make it seem like it is no big deal, even though they both know it is.

    “You should not have done so,” Agatha tells her, as she avoids looking at Rio.

    “Agatha… what happened?” Rio asks her, doing so gently because she knows that the only way she can help Agatha, which is something she is desperate to do, is if she knows what happened.

    “You know what happened, you saw the bodies, helped the souls move on,” Agatha says to Rio, clearly not wanting to talk about it. “That does not mean I know what happened,” Rio reminds Agatha. “Agatha, talk to me, Sweetheart,” Rio says, moving closer to Agatha to try and get her to talk to her “What happened?” Rio asks again, her voice a little more forceful, but still gentle.

    “I have been in this village for a few weeks, and I kept seeing her around,” Agatha explains.

    “The little girl?” Rio asks, as that’s who she assumes got this whole situation started, and Agatha nods.

    “It took me longer than it should have to notice the bruises,” Agatha admits. “You would think I would have enough experience to notice, but I did not… not at first,” Agatha explains, guilt in her voice.

    “But you did notice,” Rio says.

    “Only after I had been here for a while,” Agatha admits, clearly feeling guilty about not noticing sooner. “I told her I would help her, promised her,” Agatha tells Rio. “I learnt who were hurting her, and I trapped them, gave them what anyone who hurts a little girl deserves,” Agatha explains, a tear coming to her eyes, which Agatha quickly wipes away.

    “What happened next?” Rio asks, knowing that what happens next is what Agatha really needs to talk about, that that is what caused her to hurt herself.

    “The little girl… Charlotte, came running in, she was so happy, she released a blast of magic,” Agatha says, and Rio closes her eyes as she knows how this story is going to end, understands exactly why it would have caused Agatha to react the way she did. “She was not aiming for me, she just lost control for a moment because she was so happy to be free, but I was there and I… I…I syphoned from her,” Agatha explains, her voice breaking. “I did not mean to… I could not stop it… and then she was gone… because of me,” Agatha says, more tears falling freely from her eyes. Feeling her heart break, as Agatha in pain is something Rio absolutely hates, Rio quickly moves to Agatha’s side and once she is close enough Rio wraps both her arms around Agatha, pulling her in close.

    “I’ve got you, I’ve got you,” Rio say, as she holds Agatha. “Mother was right… I am evil… I cannot be good,” Agatha says, though her tears.

    “No Agatha, she was wrong,” Rio tells her. “Agatha, you only have your ability because of her,” Rio reveals, deciding it’s time for Agatha to know something she has come to realise Agatha doesn’t know, something that for Rio it never felt like the right time explain, at least until now. “What do you mean?” Agatha asks confused. “I have always had my ability,” Agatha says, as she assumed that was why her mother always hated her, and she remembers taking the magic of another when she was a child. “No, you have not,” Rio tells her. “Agatha when you were a child, because of what your mother was doing to you, what she had others do, what she was depriving you off, your magic took it on itself to help you stay alive,” Rio explains. “But that is a lot of magic to use all the time,” Rio explains. “And because of that I need to recharge, that is why I can take magic from others,” Agatha realises. “It is why I cannot control it, because I take what I need, and cannot stop until I have it,” Agatha realises, and Rio nods. “It is why I feel weak when I have not done so in a while,” Agatha realises, and as she does everything falls into place for her. “So, I am wrong, mother was right, I should not exist,”

    “No Agatha, you are not wrong, you are incredible,” Rio corrects. “You are a survivor, you were given horrible circumstances under the control of a horrible women, and you found a way to not just live, but thrive; that is incredible,” Rio tells Agatha.

    “Is that not an insult to your precious balance?” Agatha asks, as that’s what she assumes.

    “No, you Agatha Harkness, are human personification of the balance,” Rio tells her. “Both life and death in one person,” Rio tells her, the amazement she feels towards Agatha being perfectly clear in her voice. “Is that why you love me?” Agatha asks, moving away from Rio, but not out of her arms, hurt clear on her face. “Because I remind you of your precious balance?” Agatha asks, feeling hurt by the implications. “No,” Rio assures Agatha. “I sought you out because I wanted to understand you, understand how life and death can be so intertwined,” Rio admits, feeling that considering everything it would be best if she were honest with Agatha. “But then I met you… and for the first time in an eternity, you made me feel... human,” Rio admits, there being no other way to explain what Agatha makes her feel. “I feel in love with you, Agatha, not because of cosmic forces, but because of you, because of your beauty, and strength, your mind, your thirst for knowledge, and yes, the way you survive, but that’s just one part of what I love about you,” Rio tells Agatha. “You, Agatha Harkness, have made death want to live,” Rio tells her, and Agatha feels that is pretty amazing considering right now she doesn’t really want to live herself.

    “I am not worthy of that,” Agatha tells Rio.

    “Yes, you are,” Rio says, stressing her words, knowing she will do everything she can to help Agatha believe that. “Agatha everything your mother tried to get you to believe is wrong,” Rio assures her. “You are worthy of love, you are worthy of life, you are allowed to be your true self,” Rio promises Agatha.

    “What if I do not know who my true self is?” Agatha asks Rio. “Then we will figure it out,” Rio tells Agatha.

    “We?” Agatha asks, noticing her word choice.

    “You may have been alone for the first eighteen years of your life, but you are not alone anymore,” Rio assures Agatha. “I am here, Agatha, I love you, I see you, the real you,” Rio tells Agatha.

    “I… I do not know how to accept that,” Agatha admits. “I do not know how to accept that everything mother made me believe is not real,” Agatha admits.

    “I know,” Rio says, with an understanding look on her face. “That is why we will figure it out, together,” Rio says, as she keeps one arm around Agatha, but reaches out and takes Agatha’s hand with her other hand. “But Agatha, we can only do that if you stay alive,” Rio tells her. “I cannot completely understand the pain you are in, but I know I want to do everything I can to help you with it,” Rio tells her. “Hurting yourself…... is not the answer,” Rio tells Agatha, who, despite everything going on, can appreciate the fact that it is death herself telling her not to kill herself. “Then what is?” Agatha asks.

    “Accepting yourself, for who you are, accepting what you can do is necessary to survive, and accepting that your mother was a vengeful spiteful women who never told you a single thing that was true,” Rio tells her. “Agatha, you are a witch, you do what you have to do to survive,” Rio tells her.

    “That is exactly what I am struggling with right now,” Agatha admits. “I know,” Rio responds. “Which is exactly why I am going to do everything I can to help you,” Rio promises. “You have me, Agatha, completely, always,” Rio assures Agatha.

    “It is hard for me to trust that,” Agatha admits. “But I do want to,” Agatha reveals, and Rio knows how much of a big deal that is.

    “That is a good first step,” Rio tells Agatha, leaning down and placing a gently kiss on Agatha’s cheek as they drift into silence, as Rio continues to hold Agatha, both knowing that Agatha’s problems, the scars her mother caused, still remain, but both of them are also aware that Agatha no longer has to face her pain alone.

    “I did,” Prue says, as she gets to her feet, and pulls he her brother up to his feet. “I just knew I had to protect you both,” Prue tells her brother and mother, trying to make it seme like what she did was not a big deal. “You did, you did an amazing job,” Agatha says, before walking over to Prue and hugging her, feeling incredibly guilty that it was needed in the first place, but also realising the implication of what Prue said. “Thanks Mama,” Prue says, knowing what would have happened if she did not tackle her brother, but also feeling that she just did what she had to do so it was not a big deal.

    “Agatha? What’s wrong?” Rio asks worried, as she walks towards her wife. “If it was not for Prue I would have drained Nicky today,” Agatha reveals, guilt in his voice, as she cannot believe she came close to that. “What happened?” Rio asks, as she sits down next to her wife, doing her best to keep her worry out of her voice as she does not want Agatha to feel even guiltier than she clearly already feels.

    “We were practicing blasting, Prue did what I instructed perfectly, and then next thing I knew she was tackling Nicky, and a blast went over my head,” Agatha explains.

    August 1759 Five months have passed since Nicky almost hit Agatha with his magic, and thankfully nothing like that has happened since, and in that time Prue and Nicky have turned nine years old. As they needed supplies Agatha, Rio, Nicky, and Prue are in the local village together.

Looking around the room Prue sees her mom walk in, and so she walks over to her, pick pocking a couple of easy targets as she goes, as she could not resist.

    “Right, I did,” Rio says, sounding almost proud of that.

    “I think that just proves that I am both my mothers daughter,” Prue comments, sounding incredibly proud of that.

    “Yeah, you are,” Rio says proudly, as she kisses Prue’s head, and the two of them continue to watch Nicky sing, while Agatha cons people, the two of them working as a team, and once Nicky finishes singing the four of them quickly leave the village before anyone can realise what they are doing, having a great time as they go.

    November 1759 Three months have passed since Nicky first sang the Ballard, he created to get money from people and as it was so successful the first time it is something that has happened a few more times, at Agatha’s insistence. It is the middle of the afternoon and Prue is sick in bed while her brother, and mothers are trying to help; but in Nicky’s case due to his frail state, he is once again being kept from his sister.

    “Hi,” Rio greats, as she walks over to her daughter.

    “Hi, Mom,” Prue responds.

While Rio is telling Prue a story Agatha is gone in search of Nicky who is sitting in the garden. Walking over to him Agatha sits down with her son. “Are you alright?” Agatha asks as she sits down across from her son. “Not really,” Nicky admits. “I am just worried about Prue,” Nicky says, as he knows that Prue was weakened because she gave him magic, a lot of it. “Prue is going to be okay, Nicky,” Agatha assures her son, not realising just what Prue is doing for her brother which is causing her to be so weak. “Do you really think so?” Nicky asks, worried.

    “Yeah, I do,” Agatha says, putting her arm around Nicky and the two of them drift into silence as they sit together in the garden, both worrying about Prue.

    May 1760 Six months have passed since Prue got a pretty bad cold and in that time, Prue has been experiencing more complications from giving Nicky magic, but because she knows he needs it she refuses to stop.

    It is late at night and having checked to make sure their Mama is asleep and that their mom is as close to asleep as she gets Prue is sneaking back into hers and Nicky’s room and once she does, she walks over to her bother and shakes him awake.

    “Nicky, wake up,” Prue says, as she gently shakes him awake. “Prue?” Nicky asks confused.

    “It is time,” Prue tells her brother.

    “No, we can wait another couple of days,” Nicky says, as he does not want to cause his sister harm, as he sits up in his bed.

    “No, we cannot, you were barley able to walk today,” Prue says, and before he can object anymore, she takes a step back from her brother, and once she does, she sends a blast of magic towards her brother. Just like so many times before the purple magic goes out of Prue and turns into green magic as it goes into Nicky, but unlike other times Prue can feel her brother draining more magic, more life, than he has ever done before, and he shows no sign of stopping. “Nic… stop,” Prue begs, barely able to speak, and after a split second Nicky realises what he is doing and cuts the flow of magic, causing his sister to fall to the ground.

    “It is okay,” Prue assures him.

    “I am sorry, I am so sorry,” Nicky says, horror in his voice as he thinks about what he almost did to his sister, the person who matters more to him than anyone else in the universe.

    “Okay, we will figure something out, but until then I will give you small bursts of magic every morning and night,” Prue tells her brother. “That is not sustainable,” Nicky says worried, knowing that will quickly become too much for his sister.

    “It does not have to be, it just has to be until we can find another solution,” Prue tells her brother, who nods, and the two of them drift into silence as they sit together, Nicky feeling incredibly guilty about what he just did, while Prue knows that no matter what it takes she will find a way to save he brother, and as they sit together Señor Scratchy climbs onto Nicky’s lap. Having no idea what is going on with their kids Agatha and Rio are in bed, and while Agatha is fast asleep Rio is not and suddenly, she gasps, which wakes up Agatha.

    “Rio?” Agatha asks concerned. “What’s wrong?” Agatha asks. “I am not sure,” Rio admits, trying to figure out what is going on. “I just got the feeling like something is really wrong, but then it disappeared,” Rio admits, having not felt like that for a very long time.

    “Nicky and Prue,” Agatha says, and both of them quickly get up and hurry out of their room.

    Heading straight to Prue and Nicky’s room Agatha and Rio are both so concerned that they do not notice how loud they are being as they hurry into their kids’ room, finding Prue and Nicky sitting on Pure’s bed, holding Señor Scratchy, and both Agatha and Rio know their kids well enough to know that something is wrong.

    “What happened? What’s wrong?” Agatha asks her kids worried. “I had a nightmare,” Prue says, before her brother can say anything. “It was really bad, Nicky is helping me,” Prue explains.

    “Oh Sweetheart,” Rio says, and both she and Agatha walk over to their kids, and sit down on the bed.

    “That is okay, you do not have to, we are all here,” Rio assures her daughter, and with some difficulty due to her weakened state Prue leans forward and hugs her parents, trying to distract them from worrying about her. “I love you,” Prue tells her mothers.

    “We love you too,” Rio responds, and once they break apart Prue, who wants to feel safe, moves so she is sitting between her parents, both of whom put their arms around her, giving Prue exactly the feeling of safety she needs, while Nicky moves so he is sitting next to Agatha, who puts her other arm around him, and the four of them drift into silence as they sit together, Nicky feeling guilty, Prue feeling weak, Agatha suspecting that something more is going on, while Rio is wondering what the hell she just experienced.

    August 1760 Three months have passed since Nicky always killed his sister when he was taking magic from her and in that time, they have turned ten, and Prue has been obsessively thinking of a way to save her brother as she knows she cannot keep giving him magic every day, as it is taking a toll on both of them.

    It is late at night and as they have been on a supply run Agatha, Nicky, Prue and Señor Scratchy, are camping together while Rio is doing her job. Looking through her journal and a book she ‘borrowed’ from her mother’s collection Prue is putting the final touches on something she has been working on for a very long time, since even before her brother almost killed her.

    “This is it,” Prue mutters, and after looking between the book and note book once more time she looks over to her mama who is fast asleep, and after a moment of hesitation Prue rips a page out of her journal, putting it into her pocket and grabbing a bag of what her mother and brother think are usually supplies but which are actually different supplies she used stolen money to buy as she knew she would need them.

    Once she has everything, she needs Prue looks towards Señor Scratchy who is watching her. “This is something I have to do, be good,” Prue tells the rabbit before purposely leaving her journal on her ‘pillow’ where it will be seen before walking over to her mama who is asleep, being as quiet as possible. “I love you Mama, so much,” Prue says quietly before kissing her mother’s cheek, and after a few moments of hesitation Prue sneaks over to where her brother is.

    “Nicky, Nicky wakes up,” Prue says, gently shaking her brother awake. “Prue?” Nicky asks confused.

    “There is something we have to do,” Prue tells her brother. “We do not have long,” Prue explains, knowing that they are on a time clock. “What do you mean?” Nicky asks.

    “I cannot explain here, will you trust me?” Prue asks her brother, as she does not want to risk waking up her mother.

    “Of course,” Nicky says, standing up, as he will always trust his sister. “Kiss Mama goodbye, just in case,” Prue tells her brother and feeling incredibly confused, but trusting his sister, Nicky walks over to his mother, and gives her a gentle kiss on her cheek, and once he does Nicky walks over to his sister.

    “Let’s go,” Prue tells her brother, and forcing herself not to look back at their mother she starts walking.

    For about a minute Prue and Nicky walk, walking away from their mother, until Nicky decides they are far enough away that he can ask. “Where are we going? What are we doing?” Nicky asks his sister. “There is a clearing about five minutes this way,” Prue says, pointing in the direction. “Mama always says that being beneath the moonlight, especially during midnight on a full moon, can make magic more powerful; we are going to need to be as powerful as possible,” Prue tells her brother, having used every lesson their mothers taught them to come up with their plan. “Why? What are we doing?” Nicky asks confused.

    “Either saving you, or potentially killing us both,” Prue admits, sounding way to casual for Nicky’s liking.

    “Wait what?” Nicky asks Prue, reaching out and stopping her. “I am not going to let you kill yourself, Prue,” Nicky tells his sister. “Well, I am not going to let you die,” Prue tells her brother. “I created a ritual, it will draw on the cosmic power we both have inside of us from Mom, our connection, and use everything Mama has ever taught us to give us what we need to save you, forever,” Prue tells her brother. “What if I cannot be saved?” Nicky asks his sister, as he cannot help but think.

    “We should go back and wake Mama, so she at least knows what we are doing,” Nicky tells his sister, feeling that it is cruel to risk the possibility of Agatha waking up with both of them gone.

    “No,” Prue tells her brother, shaking her head. “Nicky Mama would do anything to save you, she would destroy the whole universe if she had to, fight Mom and everything she is, but she would not let me risk myself, would never choose between us,” Prue says, knowing that. “And risking me is the only chance we have,” Prue tells her brother.

    “What if I decide to go back to mama, and not be apart of this?” Nicky asks his sister.

    “Then I will do it alone,” Prue tells he brother. “I am not giving up on you,” Prue tells her brother. “I am not giving up on our family because we both know that if you die, and Mom has to take you, Mama will never forgive her, and that will destroy our family forever, I cannot let that happen,” Prue explains to her brother, fighting back tears as she does not want to destroy her family. “Can you honestly say that if the positions were reversed you would?” Prue asks her brother.

    “No… I would not,” Nicky realises, as just like Prue he does not want his family to be destroyed. “Prue if this does not work, we tell Mama and Mom everything, we tell them that you have been giving me magic and we figure out a solution, together,” Nicky tells his sister.

    “Deal,” Prue responds, sticking out her hand for a pinkie swear, and once they do that the two siblings continue to walk together, both feeling incredibly nervous about what they are going to do.

    After a few minutes they get to the clearing that Prue has been leading them to.

    “We have to set up in the middle of the clearing,” Prue tells her brother. “What are we setting up?” Nicky asks.

    “We are using candles, which I have also carved specific runes onto, to set up a pentagram, putting one in the middle of the pentagram, and the lines of the pentagram are going to be formed with the herbs that mama taught as are best for harnessing power,” Prue explains to her brother. “Okay,” Nicky responds.

    “What do we do now?” Nicky asks his sister.

    “We sit in the middle of the pentagram,” Prue says, dropping the bag she used to carry everything, and the two of them do just that, and once they are sitting Prue places the last candle between them before waving her hand to light all the candles. “Can you read upside down?” Prue asks her brother, as she pulls the piece of paper out of her pocket, as she thought so, but she was not sure.

    “Yeah,” Nicky says, as that is something he has been able to do for a while. “Good,” Prue says, putting the piece of paper between them, right next to the final candle, so that she can read it the right way up while it is upside down for Nicky. “We have to take hands, and on the count of three we say the spell,” Prue tells her brother.

    “Okay,” Nicky says, feeling nervous, and worried about what this will do to Prue, but also trusting her.

    “Okay,” Prue says as she takes her brothers hands, their hands over the sixth candle that is between them. “One, Two, Three,” Prue says. “Filii Mortis, Filii vitae, magicae et naturalis ordinis intertexti, in id quod sumus, haurimus, fundamentum ipsius universi, connexum et unum agendi, ut cor nostrum nobis det desiderium, ut nos salvare sinamus. fili, consec- tus, alter casus necessarius. In hoc sacro loco ac tempore omnem vitam, potestatem mortis, potentiam obtinentes, omnia trahimus quae servare non possumus. Liberi vitae, filii mortis, Mundum deprecantes, Ut nobis hoc unum damus.,” Prue and Nicky say together, and as the say the words purple magic comes out of Prue and starts to entwine them, as green magic comes out of Nicky doing the same, and once they finish the words the magic combines, there is a burst of black and white light, and as the light fades it is clear that both Nicky and Prue are gone.

    AN: Translation of the spell cast by Prue and Nicky is: Children of Death, Children of Life, magic, and the natural order intertwined, we draw on what we are, the foundation of the universe itself, connected, and acting as one, to give us our heart desire, to allow us to save the son, consequences accepted, a second chance needed. Possessing the power of life, and the power of death, the power of the universe, in this sacred place and time, we draw on everything we are to keep what we cannot allow to be. Children of life, children of death, pleading with the universe to give us this one reprieve.

    Chapter 18

    Chapter 18 AN: Sorry about all the pain in the last chapter, I wish I could say this one is less painful…. But it is not.

    Having no idea what her children have done Agatha, who was sleeping soundly, suddenly wakes up as she feels a pulse, the kind of pulse that tells her that extremely strong magic has been used. Opening her eyes, and sitting up, Agatha is incredibly confused, wondering exactly what happened, but then she realises that neither Nicky nor Prue are lying where she was went to sleep.

NICHOALS!” Agatha yells as loud as she can, and while she gets no response what she does feel is the sensation that tells her that Rio has appeared. “You!” Agatha says, sounding furious, as she turns to where Rio has appeared. “What did you do?” Agatha asks her wife, her mind going to the worse possible option, the option that Rio took not just Nicky, but both their children, onto the afterlife. “My love…” Rio starts to say.

    “No! what did you do!” Agatha exclaims, and she sends several blasts of magic towards Rio, clearly not thinking logically, and Rio easily blocks it, not fighting back herself as she knows Agatha well enough to know that right now, in this moment, she is beyond reason, something which is completely understandable.

    As she knows her wife so well Rio knows that she is not going to listen to reason right now so with a wave of her hand Rio moves Agatha so that she is against a tree, and with another wave of her hand vines come out of the ground and tie Agatha’s hands back, keeping her in position; forcing her to listen to what Rio has to say, without being able to fight back. “Agatha, listen to me, I promise you, I did not take Nicky or Prue anywhere,” Rio promises her wife, feeling hurt that Agatha would assume that, but she also understands, as she knows that Agatha has been dreading the day when Rio would have no choice but to take Nicky onto the afterlife. “I am here because I felt the same magic you did, I promise I did not take them,” Rio tells her wife.

    “You did not take them?” Agatha asks, sounding shocked, as she truly believed that, as she knew the day would come where Rio was going to take Nicky.

    “I promise you My Love, I did not take them,” Rio promises, and the shock on Agatha’s face turns into a look of pure devastation.

    “If you did not take them, where are they?” Agatha asks, feeling dread as she wonders where their kids could be, as she feels horrified about what could have happened to them.

    “I do not know,” Rio says, as she waves her hand to get rid of the vines holding Agatha, feeling that Agatha is able to listen to reason now. “What do you mean you do not know where they are?” Agatha asks her wife, sounding shocked as she is not used to Rio not knowing something. “You know everything,” Agatha says to her, as she knows that Rio has always been able to tell where she and her kids are, something which has given her comfort.

    “That is usually true, but I cannot tell right now,” Rio admits, the worry she is being clear in her voice, as she cannot imagine what could have made it possible for her not to be able to tell where her kids are. “I can tell that they are alive, and together, but I do not know where they are,” Rio admits, as for her it feels like their connection has been dulled so she cannot tell much. “All I know for sure is that they are not here,” Rio explains to her wife. “I felt the ripple of magic, then I knew that they were not here, so I came straight to you,” Rio explains to her wife, as she had hoped Agatha knew what was going on, but to her horror she realises that Agatha is just as confused as she is, looking around and as she does, she notices something. “Ripple of magic, that is what woke me up,” Agatha says, trying to put together the pieces of what could have happened. “Do you think it was them?” Agatha asks.

    “Would make sense,” Rio says, as she picks up Prue’s journal. “Is that Prue’s?” Agatha asks, walking over to her wife, knowing that Prue always has her journal with her, so she must have left it for a reason. “Yeah,” Rio says, flicking through the pages, trying to get some idea about what is going on, and as she does, something catches her eye. “Agatha, listen to this,” Rio says before reading the entry that has caught her eye; May 17, 1760 It happened today, the one thing I have been worrying about since I realised what was going on, today when I gave Nicky magic, he took too much. I could feel my life slipping away, I thought it was it, but then Nicky was able to stop himself. I know giving magic is how Nicky is alive, and I will continue to give it to him, but I need to figure out another option; for both of our sake, and for Mom and Mama.

    “Prue has been giving Nicky magic?” Rio asks Agatha, looking surprised, as she had no idea, and she cannot imagine Agatha knowing about that and not telling her.

    “Sounds like it… he must be able to syphon like me,” Agatha says, feeling guilty about both the fact that Prue has been doing that and that she never realised. “How did we not realise?” Agatha asks, feeling incredibly guilty, and hating herself because of that.

    “I have no idea,” Rio says, flicking through the book to the last page where there is a page that starts addressed to them. “She left a note,” Rio realises, and the two of them start to read.

    Dear Mom and Mama, If you are reading this then something went wrong with my plan, or it was completely successful in a way I did not expect, either way, I am sorry you are finding out like this. I did not want to burden you with what I knew unless there was no other option.

    I guess I should start at the beginning, for our entire lives, in fact I think it may have even started before we were born I have been giving Nicky magic to keep him alive, when we were younger it was fine, I just needed to sleep a little more, but as we got older Nicky needed more magic, and I kept giving it to him, but it is starting to take its toll, and I do not know how much longer I will be able to use my magic to keep him alive and still be able to function myself.

    For a while I have been trying to work out a way to save Nicky, and I have created a ritual. It will draw on the cosmic magic Nicky and I have inside of us and use runes to give us what is needed to save Nicky. I do not know exactly how it will work, but I believe that it will allow us to save Nicky. Mom, Mama, I know we have kept a lot from you, but you need to know that everything I have done it has been to save Nicky because I cannot lose my brother, I cannot let our family be destroyed. We both love you, and I have used everything you have taught us to give us the best chance at succeeding. My plan is to have our ritual set up in the clearing seven minutes north from where you are Mama at midnight. Mom, Mama, I love you so much, so does Nicky.

    Love Prue.

    “There is so much we did not realise,” Agatha says, guilt in her voice, as she cannot believe she was so clueless.

    “I know,” Rio says, also feeling incredibly guilty. “Which is exactly why we are going to find them, and make it clear they can tell us everything,” Rio says, having hope that they will find their children, even if she cannot feel them.

    “Yeah, we will,” Agatha says, as she picks up Señor Scratchy and puts him in the bag she is holding. “We start in the clearing and go from there,” Agatha tells her wife.

    “And not give up until we find them,” Rio says, Agatha nods, and they start to collect everything they need.

    Once Agatha and Rio have everything, they needed collected they both hurry North, heading in the direction where they will find the clearing. As soon as the two of them get closer to the clearing they can both ‘feel’ the magic.

    “Whatever they did was incredibly powerful,” Agatha realises, as she is not sure she has ever felt what she is currently feeling.

    “I would say that is an understatement,” Rio admits, as she and Agatha continue to walk and as they walk toward the centre, she realises something. “Burnt out pentagram,” Rio says, looking around, noticing what has happened to the grass once they get close enough.

    “Definitely the right place,” Agatha says, as she starts to check the burnt- out candles for the runes that have been carved. “Runes for Time, Soul, Mind, Space, Reality, and Power,” Agatha reads, a feeling of dread rising up inside of her, as she realises just what Prue and Nicky could have tapped into and how dangerous that is. “Did they unintentionally tap into the power of the infinity stones?” Agatha asks, as Prue’s note did not mention anything about doing it on purpose, which tells her that if they did tap into the power of the infinity stones then it was on accident, which is both incredible and horrifying.

    “Before now I would say that it would be impossible to tap into the power of the stones without being in possession of them,” Rio admits. “But as Prue and Nicky are the children of a cosmic being that is exactly what they could have done, even without meaning to,” Rio explains, as like Agatha she doubts that tapping into the stones was on purpose and as she does, she feels dread rise up inside of her as she realises what that could mean. “If they have it means they could be anywhere in the universe… or in any time period,” Rio says, absolute horror rising up inside of her as she realises just how difficult it is going to be to find their children.

    “Rio? My love, talk to me,” Agatha says, getting out of bed, and walking towards Rio who is, in her Death Form, huddled in a corner with her arms around her legs. “What’s wrong?” Agatha asks, feeling terrified for Rio, but also being cautious as she does not know how Rio is going to react, and she does not want to do anything that will result in Rio feeling guilty. “They’re back, they’re all back,” Rio says, as she starts hitting her head with her hand, causing Agatha to feel terrified and she hurries towards her, forgetting all about being cautious, as all she cares about is Rio. “I can feel it! it’s too much! It’s too much!” Rio says as she goes to hit her head again, but Agatha reaches out and grabs her hands, stopping her as she squats down in front of her.

    “It’s too much, it’s too much,” Rio says, sounding like it causing her pain, which it is. “Agatha, make it stop!” Rio begs, as even when everyone was snapped away, she has never felt anything like this, as she is currently feeling like she is being teared apart from the inside.

I don’t…” Agatha starts to say, searching her mind for something that might work, feeling desperate as she knows she will do whatever she can to help her wife. “I have an idea,” Agatha says, and without letting go of Rio’s hands Agatha recites an incarnation, and to her relief as soon as she finishes the words Rio looks like she is in less pain.

Where are your parents?” The Doctor asks, and because she knows Nicky needs help now, and that she does not have the answers everyone will want Prue takes a step closer to the doctor, and remembering everything her mama taught her, Prue reaches out and puts her hand against the side of his head, attempting something she has never done before.

    Chapter 21: AN: Thank you so much for the support. Hope you like this chapter. Next one will be in about 24 hours.

    Eighteen days have passed since Prue and Nicky’s spell brough them to 2023 and while Nicky has been getting the medical treatment he needs to save his life Prue, who also received some basic medical care including all the vaccinations she needs that have been created in the last two hundred years, has been able to, due to the chaos of everything that is going on, stay in an on-call room at the hospital, which has allowed her to stay close to her brother.

    It is early in the morning and Prue, who has been borrowing clothes and everything else she needs, is walking into the hospital room where Nicky has spent the previous eighteen days.

    “Morning,” Prue greats, as she walks into her brother’s hospital room, who looks glad to see her. “How was breakfast this morning?” Prue asks her brother, as how different food is is something both of them are struggling to get used to; even more so than the all the new technology. “Odd, eggs taste very different now,” Nicky informs his sister. “You are telling me,” Prue says as she sits down on the edge of her brother’s bed. “One of the nurses gave me something called cereal for breakfast… it was odd,” Prue tells her brother, still not sure what to think about that.

    “Did it at least taste good?” Nicky asks curious.

    “Yeah, it did,” Prue confirms. “How are you feeling?” Prue asks. “Better than I have ever felt,” Nicky admits. “They have finished with the medications they call steroids, and antibiotics, I no longer have to use oxygen, and the Doctor said I will have one final treatment in that tissue repairing machine this afternoon,” Nicky tells his sister. “That is amazing,” Prue tells he brother, feeling amazed, as while she hoped this would happen there was a part of her that was too scared to truly believe.

    “Yep, the doctors are shocked, they said that with my lung and heart damage I should not have lived long after I was born,” Nicky tells Prue, as apparently his lungs we very underdeveloped and his heart had tissue damage. “Thank you,” Nicky tells his sister, as he knows he would not have lived as long as he has if it wasn’t for his sister.

    “You never have to thank me,” Prue assures him.

    “I want to,” Nicky admits. “And look,” Nicky says, and just like they have both seen their mom do many times Nicky causes a flower to appear in his hand. “I can use more of my magic,” Nicky tells his sister, sounding thrilled, and proud, about that.

    “That is great,” Prue says as she reaches out and takes the flower, realising that it is his mama’s favourite flower, the same flower they have watched their mom conjure for her many, many times. “Have you noticed anything else?” Prue asks curious.

    “I have not tried blasting,” Nicky admits.

    “Probably a good idea,” Prue admits, as considering he now has access to more of his powers it is a possibility that Nicky would be overwhelmed. “Yeah, I do not know if it is anything, but I feel like I know what is going to happen, or what should happen, more,” Nicky admits, still trying to get used to those sensations, as he is not exactly sure what they mean. “It could be, Mom and Mama always suspected that you might have some divination powers,” Prue tells his brother.

    “True,” Nicky confirms. “Once I have my last treatment, we can focus on trying to find Mom and Mama,” Nicky tells Prue, who tenses. “Nicky, it’s been 263 years, we do not know… “Prue starts to say, and Nicky realises what she is thinking.

    “Mom cannot die,” Nicky reminds his sister, cutting her off before she can say what she is going to say. “And Mama is incredibly powerful, they are out there somewhere, I know it, we just have to find them,” Nicky says, truly believing that, having complete faith in their mothers. “Do you not want to?” Nicky asks, feeling confused, wondering why Prue seems so hesitant.

    “Of course I do,” Prue tells her brother, without hesitation. “Then what are you worried about?” Nicky asks confused, and Prue avoids looking at him. “Prue, talk to me,” Nicky tells his sister, in a gentle voice, wondering what is going on with her.

    “I am worried that they are going to hate me,” Prue says in a quite voice, barely loud enough for her brother to hear.

    “Why would you think they would hate you?” Nicky asks confused, as he cannot imagine their mothers ever hating either of them.

    “Because it has been two hundred and sixty-three years,” Prue says. “Because I created, and performed, a ritual that took us from them,” Prue says. “They would not have stopped looking for us, they would have never given up, and I did that to them, I caused them that pain,” Prue says, guilt in her voice, as she has spent a lot of the last eighteen days thinking about the effects the spell she decided to cast would have had on their mothers, and she knows that whatever pain, whatever horrors, they have gone through over the past two and a half centuries is because of her. “You did that, we did it, to save me, they will understand,” Nicky assures his sister. “They are just going to be happy that we are back together,” Nicky admits, believing, just like his sister, that their mothers are somewhere, looking for them.

    “I am still going to find a way to make it up to them,” Prue says, having no idea how she is going to do so but feeling determined to do so. “Okay,” Nicky says, realising that there is no point to try to talk her sister out of that. “Prue, do you think Mom is okay with everything that has happened recently?” Nicky asks curious, as even with everything they have been trying to get used to even they understand that some pretty cosmic things have happened recently.

    “Honestly… I do not know,” Prue admits. “I think it could explain why she has not been able to sense that we are here,” Prue admits. “That would make sense,” Nicky realises. “I think she is with Mama; I think she and Mama are together and Mama is helping her,” Nicky tells his sister.

    “I think so too,” Prue admits, truly believing that their mothers are still together. “I miss them so much… I cannot even imagine how much they miss us,” Prue admits, once again feeling a rush of guilt, as she knows that for the two of them it has only been two weeks since they saw their mothers, but for their mothers it’s been over two and a half centuries. “Me either,” Nicky admits, and the two siblings drift into silence as they sit together.

    For a few minutes Prue and Nicky sit in comfortable silence until they hear the door to the room open and they both turn to look at it where they see Sharon Davis, who has visited more than once, walk in, and as soon as she sees her Prue hides the flower Nicky made in her pocket so that she does not have to explain where it came from.

    “Knock Knock,” Sharon greats.

    “Hi Sharon,” Nicky and Prue great, both feeling reassured by her presence as she has been so kind to them, and hasn’t asked too many questions about why they are so ‘different’.

    “Well hello, how are you feeling today?” Sharon asks, as she looks between the twins.

    “Good,” Prue answers.

    “Stronger,” Nicky admits.

    “That is very good to hear,” Sharon tells them, smiling at that. “I hear that you are out of here tomorrow,” Sharon says to Nicky.

    “That is the plan,” Nicky responds.

    “Well, I have been talking to your social worker and she explained that because of everything that is going on, everything that has happened, they are having some difficulty finding a placement for you until your parents can be found,” Sharon reveals, causing Nicky and Prue to exchange looks as, considering everything, they have been giving as little information as possible about their mothers. “Because of that If it is okay with the two of you, I was wondering if you would like to come stay with me and Mr Davis in Westview,” Sharon offers, as since almost hitting Prue and Nicky with her car she feels the need to look after them, to make sure they are okay. “That would great, thank you,” Nicky says, before Prue can object, as that is exactly what she was going to do, and she gives him a ‘what the hell are you thinking?’ look, but Nicky gives her a look back that says, ‘trust me,’. “Yes, thank you,” Prue responds, feeling incredibly confused about her brother.

    “Oh, that is amazing! I will go do some shopping to get you things you need. Do you have any requests?” Sharon asks, as she looks between them. “No, but thank you,” Nicky says, and Prue shakes her head. “Great! I will see you first thing in the morning!” Sharon says, looking thrilled. “I promise, I will do everything I can to help you find your parents,” Sharon assures the twins.

    “Thank you,” Prue responds, though she is pretty sure that there isn’t much Sharon is going to be able to do, and in response Sharon gives her, and then Nicky, a quick hug before leaving the room.

    As soon as Sharon leaves the room, and the door closes, Prue turns to her brother.

    “Okay, what was that?” Prue asks, feeling confused. “Not even ten minutes ago you were saying how we had to focus on finding Mom and Mama,” Prue tells her brother, confused about the way he is acting. “Which is exactly why we need to go to Westview,” Nicky tells his sister. “I know it does not make sense, but I know we need to go there, that it is what is best,” Nicky tells his sister.

    “Did you see something?” Prue asks, knowing that would tell them a lot. “Not exactly… it was more of a feeling telling me that we have to go to Westview,” Nicky admits, not sure if he is explaining things in the best way. “Please Prue, can you just trust me like I have always trusted you?” Nicky asks his sister, a level of pleading to his voice.

    “Of course,” Prue says, as she can see that it means a lot to her brother. “Thank you,” Nicky says gratefully.

    “No need, you have given me an incredibly amount of trust, the least I can do is give you the same back,” Prue tells her brother. “So, your last treatment tonight, is it in that machine?” Prue asks her brother. “Yeah, the one the doctors keep saying it was a gift form something called Stark Industries, apparently that makes it a big deal,” Nicky tells his sister, as the way the doctors say the name makes it seem like it should be something he should know.

    “It is a big deal, it saved you,” Prue tells her brother, who smiles. “Have you figured out how to work the TV?” Prue asks curious.

    “Kind of,” Nicky says and once he does Prue moves so that she is sitting next to her brother, and once they are sitting together, they watch the TV until Nicky has to go to his treatment.

    After a night where she did not get much sleep as she was worried about why her brother is so insistent they go to Westview, Prue has once again got up early, had a shower, which is an invention she very much likes, and got ready, had breakfast which was thankfully a little more like food she was used to before heading to her brothers hospital room.

    “You are ready,” Prue, who is carrying a bag of things she has been given, says as she walks into the room where she finds her brother sitting on the bed, fully dressed, with a bag next to him.

    “Yep, the doctors have already given me the all clear,” Nicky tells his sister. “Apparently I am perfectly healthy,” Nicky reveals.

    “That’s incredible,” Prue says amazed, as this is everything she wanted. “So, we are going to Westview?” Prue checks, wanting to make sure Nicky is sure about it being the right thing to do as she knows there is time, that they could use to disappear, before Sharon arrives.

    “We have to,” Nicky tells his sister. “I know you do not feel what I feel, but I promise you Prue, we need to go there,” Nicky tells his sister, a level of pleading to his voice, as he needs his sister to agree.

    “I believe you,” Prue assures him. “But that means we do not know what we are going to be facing, so we have to stick together, deal?” Prue asks her brother, sticking out her hand to do a pinkie swear.

    “Deal,” Nicky responds, and the two of them do a pinkie square. “Knock knock,” Sharon’s voice says, walking into the room, and both twins turn to look at her. “I have just spoken to the doctors Nicholas you have officially been discharged; how does it feel?” Sharon asks. “Good,” Nicky admits. “I think I am ready to leave this hospital,” Nicky admits.

    “That is good to hear,” Sharon responds. “Now, I know you both want to find your parents, and I will do everything I can to help you with that, but until we can find them I want you to know that I am here for you, I will look after you, you have a home with me and Mr Davis,” Sharon says, looking between Prue and Nicky, wanting to make that clear. “Thank you, Sharon, you have no idea how much we appreciate your kindness,” Prue tells her.

    “Oh, my dear, you never have to thank me,” Sharon assures her. “Are you ready to go?” Sharon asks, looking between them.

    “Yes,” Nicky says, and Prue nods.

    “Then let’s get this show on the road,” Sharon says, and feeling incredibly nervous both Nicky and Prue pick up the bags that hold the few possessions they have been given and follow Sharon out of the hospital room, neither twin moving far away from the other.

    A little while after they left the hospital Nicky and Prue are in the back of Sharon’s car driving through Westview.

    “Does this make you feel sick?” Nicky asks Prue in a quiet voice, trying to push down not the feeling of sickness he is feeling, but also the fear he is feeling.

    “Yep,” Prue responds, just as quietly, as apart from when they flew, something which feels very different, she has never moved this fast. “I know the town does not look like much, but I promise you it has charm,” Sharon tells Nicky and Prue, as their car overtakes a red one that is driving slowly through town.

    “The town looks lovely, Sharon,” Prue assures her. “Very different from where we are from,” Prue says, knowing that the entire world is different to where she and Nicky are from.

    “Oh? Where is that?” Sharon asks, and both Nicky and Prue panic for a second.

    “Salem,” Nicky quickly says, it being the first place he can think to say. “Oh, I have heard it is lovely there!” Sharon comments excited. “It can be,” Prue says, choosing a diplomatic answer, as Sharon pulls into a driveway.

    “Here we are, home sweet home,” Sharon says, before turning to look at her. “And even if you are not here long, I want you to think of this place as home, for as long as you are,” Sharon tells them.

    “We will,” Nicky tells her, as the three of them get out of the car. “Mr Davis is at work, but he will be home tonight and is very much looking forward to seeing you,” Sharon says, as they walk towards the house. “We are looking forward to seeing him too,” Nicky says, as they walk into the house, and as soon as they do both he and Prue are overwhelmed by how different everything is.

    “How about we start with a tour,” Sharon suggests, but before she can start on that tour Prue feels a title wave of magic, because of the intensity of what she is feeling Prue reaches out and grabs her brothers hand without even thinking, and as the magic washes over them everything changes, and even more confusing everything turns black and white.

    “I do not know,” Prue admits, though she knows she has never felt anything like that. “Sharon? Are you okay?” Prue asks concerned.

    “Of course, you are Prudence and Nicholas, I am looking after you until your parents pick you up,” Sharon says. “Why don’t I go get us some lemonade,” Sharon says before heading into the kitchen.

    “Okay, what is going on?” Nicky asks Prue, hoping she knows as he certainly does not.

    “I do not know, all I know is I have never felt power like that,” Prue admits. “Is this why you said we had to come to Westview?” Prue asks. “I am not sure,” Nicky admits. “Let’s see what we can find out from the house, everything has changed there might be some clues,” Nicky tells his sister.

    “Good plan,” Prue responds, and the two of them start to search. As their children are arriving in Westview, not that they know that Agatha is sitting on the couch in their cottage when Rio walks into the cottage, arriving home after doing her job.

    “How are things out there?” Agatha asks her wife when she sees her. “Still chaotic,” Rio admits. “People are struggling, people are hurting, and it is causing a lot of death,” Rio admits, as she walks over to Agatha and sits down next to her, it being clear that Rio is exhausted.

    “I am sorry,” Agatha tells her, being able to tell that Rio is in pain. “How are you doing? Is everything in your mind still a lot?” Agatha asks, as she reaches out and takes Rio’s hand.

    “Yes, but it is starting to settle down,” Rio admits.

    “Good, that’s good,” Agatha tells her.

    “I am surprised you are not in the basement,” Rio admits, as that is where she assumed she would find Agatha when she got home.

    “I needed a bit of a break,” Agatha admits.

    “It is good that you are recognizing that,” Rio says, as usually she has to drag Agatha away from the Darkhold, something which is concerning. “I know,” Agatha says, leaning over and kissing Rio’s cheek, and as she pulls back she realises something. “Did you feel that?” Agatha asks, having felt a truly intense sensation.

    “I am not sure,” Rio admits, as she felt something but she is not sure what. “What did it feel like to you?” Rio asks.

    “The Afterglow of multiple spells being cast at once, layered, working in tandem… would have taken someone pretty powerful,” Agatha says, feeling amazed, as her mind goes straight to how she can use the power to find Prue and Nicky. “Feel like joining me on a little trip to New Jersey?” Agatha asks her wife.

    “Are you asking me on a date?” Rio asks amused.

    “A mystery to solve, an extremely powerful witch, of course it is a date, what do you say?” Agatha asks.

    “I say that sounds like it is exactly what we need,” Rio says, leaning forward kissing her wife, and once they break apart, they start to make their way to Westview, as quickly as possible.
