December 2015 For Agatha and Rio, a lot has changed over the over three hundred years they have been together, but same sex marriage being legalized is something they did not expect to actually happen as they experienced so much hate due to who they were to ever even hope that the world would become evolved enough for not just acceptance, but a world where they would be embraced.

    As their mother is travelling to Eastern Europe Nicky and Prue are still sitting in the ‘office’ as Lilia is getting them food, with Agatha. While Nicky has continued to read his mothers notes Prue is sitting crossed legged on the ground, very much looking like she is mediating.

    “What are you doing?” Nicky asks his sister, trying to figure out what is going on, as while he is reasonably sure that she is not meditating, as that would be very unlike his sister, he is confused about what she is doing. “You and Mama have been saying that I am connected to magic, I am trying to see just what I can sense,” Prue explains to her brother. “You are trying to determine what is going on with Mama and Wanda,” Nicky realises, wondering if his sister is going to succeed. “I am,” Prue responds, trying to focus and as she does, seconds later, she lets out a heartbreaking scream that cause Lilia and Agatha to come running into the room from the kitchen, both of them clearly incredibly confused about what could have just happened.

    “What do you mean what happens next?” Wanda asks confused. “I’m dead, I assume that means I have to move on to the Afterlife,” Wanda says to Rio. “Not necessarily,” Rio tells Wanda. “You see you are dead, which is very inconvenient for me, because I need you to reverse the spell you put on Agatha,” Rio tells Wanda, who is confused about how Rio is acting. “You are Death, and you are so concerned about one human,” Wanda says to Rio, giving her a pondering look as she tries to understand her. “Because she is my love, my heart, my soul, my everything,” Rio tells Wanda, who can’t help but think of Vision.

    “She’s evil,” Wanda says, and because this is where she is in control Rio is able to use magic to knock Wanda off her feet.

    “Agatha Harkness is a lot of things, evil is not one of them,” Rio says angrily, as Wanda pushes herself back up to her feet. “Actually, I can’t believe you can’t see just how similar you are,” Rio admits. “We are nothing alike!” Wanda exclaims, and Rio once again ushes her magic to push Wanda back to the ground. “I am nothing like her!” Wanda exclaims, clearly getting frustrated with Rio constantly knocking her down. “You don’t know her, not really, you just see what she wants people to believe because it’s her way of protecting herself, so let me educate you,” Rio says, once again using her magic to keep Wanda down. “Agatha was born to an abusive mother, in a time that could never understand her, and because of that she was almost executed due to people’s fear,” Rio tells Wanda. “She taught me what real, unconditional, love was, and I taught her the same. I taught her what I was like to be truly safe, because her mother made sure she never remembered what that was like,” Rio explains. “Our love was so pure, so true, that it created twins… sounds familiar?” Rio asks, and she can tell Wanda is shocked by that. “Like yours our twins were lost to us at ten years old, for over two hundred and sixty years, we searched, and just like you Agatha turned to the Darkhold for answers, and we were both willing to do whatever we had to do to be reunited with our children,” Rio explains, and Wanda sees too many similarities for her liking. “But then do you know what happened?” Rio asks, and Wanda shakes her head, not trying to get up again as she is truly interested in what Rio is saying. “Our twins found us, they were brough through time and space to Westview,” Rio explains, not realising that Wanda is starting to feel angry that Rio and Agatha get to be reunited with their children, but she does not. “We’ve finally got them back, but their Mama doesn’t remember them, no matter what I tell her every few days she forgets them, and they are heartbroken, because of you,” Rio explains to Wanda, tying to keep a hold of her anger. “I know how much you want your boys back, I understand what you are feeling, what you are willing to do to get them back, because for over two hundred years I was you. Wanda, I will help you get your boys back,” Rio says, being willing to do that even though it goes against everything she is, even though it will lead to consequences she cannot predict. “But only if you give Agatha back to me, back to our kids,” Rio tells Wanda, who tries to hide how tempted she is by the offer. “My boys are gone,” Wanda tells Rio.

    “Do you really believe that?” Rio asks, as Wanda slowly stands up, Rio not stopping her this time.

    “No,” Wanda admits. “But if they are alive then I want them to be proud of me, not horrified by what I’ve done in their name,” Wanda says, planning on finding another way to be reunited with her boys. “I am sorry for your children, they are innocent, but Agatha is not, I will not give her back you,” Wanda says, and then before Rio can stop her, truly believing that she will be with her children again, when she deserves to be, Wanda runs through the green portal, knowing that when she see her boys again, she will make sure they can be proud of her.

    “NO!” Rio yells feeling her heart break, as she knows that with Wanda going though that portal, out of her reach, the spell on Agatha cannot be broken.

    Having no idea where she is going, but believing that, when she deserves to be, she will find her way back to her boys, Wanda makes her way through the green portal, and for a few moments, or at least that is what it seems like, Wanda feels at complete peace, she feels free, like she is weightless; but then it is like she slams into the ground.

    “Ouch,” Wanda says, as between the way Rio threw her around, and this latest blow Wanda is feeling sore. “Didn’t think I would still feel pain,” Wanda mutters to herself, and as she pushes herself up she realises that there is a woman, a very old, very powerful woman, standing before her. “Um, hi,” Wanda greats, feeling nervous as she can feel deep inside of herself that the woman standing before her deserves respect. “Hello,” the women greats.

    “I’m Wanda,” Wanda says as she slowly gets to her feet.

    “I’m Hecate,” Hecate says, and because she hasn’t studied a lot of magic Wanda does not realise how much of a big deal that is. “Current Goddess of Magic,” Hecate explains, feeling the need to do so after seeing the confused look on Wanda’s face.

    “Current?” Wanda asks confused, having noticed the word choice and having spent enough time around Natasha Romanoff to know that word choices are important.

    “Everything has it’s season, mine will eventually end,” Hecate says. “And when I do, I already know who will take my place,” Hecate says, and as she sees the look on Wanda’s face she chuckles. “Do not worry my child, it is not you, will never be you,” Hecate assures her. “You are on a different path,” Hecate says as she sticks her hand out for Wanda to take. “Come my child, your journey is far from over,” Hecate tells Wanda, who follows the Goddess of Magic, trying to comprehend everything.

    After watching Wanda go through to where she cannot follow Rio collapses to her knees, knowing that Wanda is taking her hope of being able to break the spell on Agatha with her. Feeling tears roll down her face Rio has no idea how she is going to face Nicky and Prue, how she is going to tell them that she couldn’t do what they needed her to do.

    For a while Rio honestly having no idea how long, Rio just lets the tears roll, feels the devastation and guilt, until everything she is feeling, all the hurt, turns into a burning fire deep inside of her. “I will find another way,” Rio promises, and as she knows, even if it is painful, that she has to face Prue, and Nicky, that they need to know what has happened, Rio forces herself to stand up, and makes her way home.

    Not long after she left Mount Wundagore, or at least the version of that exists between Life and Death, Rio arrives back in Westview. Hating herself for the devastation she going to cause her children Rio makes her way inside.

    Walking inside Rio sees Lilia and Agatha in the living room, but no sign of Prue or Nicky.

    “They’re upstairs,” Lilia tells Rio, knowing exactly what she is going to tell Nicky and Prue as Prue has already realised and told her. “Thank you,” Rio says, and forcing herself not to look at Agatha, Rio heads upstairs.

    Getting upstairs Rio goes straight to Nicky and Prue’s room, where she gently knocks on the door.

    “Come in,” Nicky’s voice says so Rio takes a moment to prepare herself before walking into the room, as she walks into the room, she isn’t surprised to find Prue sitting in the window ledge and Nicky sitting on the ground next to her, as she knows they both like to sit there. “Hi Mom,” Nicky greats, and Rio walks over and sits down across from them, leaning against Prue’s bed. “Are you okay?” Nicky asks his mother, feeling concerned about her.

    “Not really, but I’m not hurt,” Rio admits, feeling torn between not wanting to lie to her kids, and not wanting them to worry more than they already are. “Nicky, Prue, Wanda’s…” Rio starts to say.

    “Dead,” Prue finishes, wanting to save her mother from needing to give the full explanation as she cannot imagine it would be easy for her. “We know,” Prue tells her mother.

    “You do?” Rio asks, not as surprised as she probably should be. “I felt her magic disappear from the World, knew that it meant she died, even without Nicky confirming it,” Prue tells her mother, as she continues to stare out the window, knowing that even if she tried, she wouldn’t be able to explain how it feels to know Wanda’s chaos magic is no longer in the world, so she is not even going to try.

    “Oh,” Rio says, not sure how to respond to that. “I’m really sorry that you felt that,” Rio says, looking between her children, suspecting that they are going to need to talk to it a bit more when everything is not so ‘raw’. “I am still feeling it,” Prue admits, and she turns away from the window to look at her mother. “Do you think we will find another way to break the spell on Mama?” Prue asks her mother, as while she has a plan on her own, she wants to know what her mother thinks, as plans she comes up with on her own have a habit of not turning out like expected.

    “I do,” Rio admits, not sure if she truly knows or if it is what she needs to believe. “I don’t know what it is, or how long it will take to find it, but I know that I am not going to give up until I find a way,” Rio tells her children. “No matter what it takes,” Rio tells her children and just as Prue is about to tell her mother her plan Nicky, with a vacant look on his face, shakes his head at his sister, telling her not to, but after a second the look is gone and Prue has enough experience with her brothers divination abilities to know he will have no idea what he just did.

    “I read some more of Mama’s notes while you were gone, apart from just being fascinating, I think they might be useful, I think that we might be able to find something to help,” Nicky tells his mother, as while he isn’t certain everything seems to indicate that the notes, they found will be very useful. “I hope we can,” Rio tells her children. “I am so sorry that I couldn’t make Wanda give Mama back to us,” Rio tells her children, looking between them and feeling extremely guilty that she couldn’t give her children what they want most.

    “It is okay Mom, it is not your fault,” Prue assures her, repeating her mothers words back at her. “Wanda made the decision not to remove the spell on Mama; now we just have to find a different way,” Prue tells her, knowing she already knows the different way.

    “You have nothing to feel guilty about, we have not failed Mama, the only way we could is if we stop trying, if we give up on getting her back,” Nicky tells his mother.

    “Which we are never going to do,” Rio says to her children, as she knows that she and Agatha never once agave up on getting Nicky and Prue back, now the three of them can never give up on getting Agatha back. “Never,” Prue confirms.

    “Never ever,” Nicky confirms, and the three of them drift into silence as they sit together, all three of them thinking about how much they want Agatha back, and what they are willing to do.

    Hours after she got home Rio, still trying to deal with everything that happened, is walking Agnes home, there being a small part of her that hopes that now that Wanda is gone the spell will suddenly break on its own, returning Agatha to her.

    “You’re quiet,” Agnes says to Rio.

    “I have a lot on my mind,” Rio responds, trying to make it seem like it is no big deal.

    “Are you mad at me?” Agnes asks, trying to make sense of what she is experiencing from her perspective. “Did I do something?” Agatha asks, a level of vulnerability to her voice that Rio knows Agatha with her memories doesn’t always show.

    “No, of course not,” Rio tells her. “I… I just, have a lot going on with my job,” Rio says, knowing that that is not technically a complete lie. “Well… I could make you feel better,” Agnes says, moving closer to Rio and attempting to kiss her but Rio turns her head so that Agatha kisses her cheek as while she is desperate to feel Agatha’s lips on hers once more, she will not allow that to happen when Agatha is not herself. “Right… something is wrong,” Agnes realises. “Why are you lying to me? What are you keeping from me?” Agnes asks, clearly hurt that, from her perspective, Rio is keeping so much from her.

    “I am lying because you won’t accept the truth, you can’t,” Rio tells Agnes, giving her a bitter laugh. “Damn it, Agnes, do you think I like this? Do you think I like keeping things from you? I don’t. I would give anything to be able to tell you everything I am not saying and have you believe me, but you won’t, believe me I’ve tried,” Rio says, the frustration and pain she is feeling being perfectly clear in her voice.

    “So what? You’re just going to give up?” Agnes asks, and Rio gets a look of pure anger on her face.

    “Never say that!” Rio grows. “Everything I am doing is because I will never give up on you, never give up on us, never give up on our family,” Rio grows. “Don’t you dare doubt that!” Rio says angrily. “I’m sorry,” Agnes says, not understanding everything, but understand enough to know that she has unintentionally hurt Rio. “What can I do?” Agnes asks, and Rio takes a few moments to calm herself.

    “Nothing, you’ll forget we had this fight soon enough,” Rio says, though she knows she will remember. “You should probably go inside,” Rio tells her.

    “Okay, are you sure you don’t want to come inside?” Agnes asks. “It’s better I don’t,” Rio admits. “I’ll see you tomorrow,” Rio says, and hearing that Agnes nods before heading into the house, Rio watching her until she is safely inside the house.

    After making sure that Agatha is safely inside Rio walks back to the house she shares with Nicky, Prue, and Lilia. Walking into the house Rio knows that her children are in bed, and so she walks into the living room where Lilia is.

    “I’ve got a double ready for you,” Lilia says, when she sees Rio. “Right now, I think I need a triple,” Rio says, as while alcohol doesn’t have much effect on her she very much likes the taste, as she walks over to where Lilia is.

    “Are you okay?” Lilia asks, as Rio sits down next to her. “No,” Rio admits. “I really thought I could convince Wanda to reverse the spell,” Rio admits, guilt in her voice, as she accepts the drink from Lilia. “What happened?” Lilia asks curious.

    “She chose to move on, to not commit anymore horrors in her children’s names,” Rio explains.

    “That would have been a difficult choice to make,” Lilia realises. “Incredibly so,” Rio admits. “And now Nicky and Prue are suffering,” Rio says. “It’s not fair,” Rio says, her voice breaking, “No, it’s not,” Lilia confirms, and moments after she does Rio feels a very familiar tug, and she knows exactly what she has to do.

    “I’ve go to go,” Rio says as she stands up. “I still have a job to do,” Rio tells Lilia.

    “I’ll see you when you get back, so will Prue and Nicky,” Lilia says, trying to reminder of the good, and Rio nods before leaving.

    Not long after Rio left, while her brother sleeps in the bed next to her, Prue, being as quiet as possible, as she knows that what she is going to do is something she needs to do alone, gets up. Squatting down next to her bed Prue reaches beneath it and pulls out a trunk.

    Once she has the trunk Prue sneaks out of her room, knowing that this is something she needs to do alone. Heading out of her room Prue heads down to the basement, being extra quiet as she sneaks past Lilia’s room. After getting to the basement Prue sets up the candles in a circle, a circle she sits in the centre off.

    “Here goes nothing,” Prue mutters to herself, dedicating her entire focus into doing what she knows she wants to happen as she recites a spell that she has been working on for several months, knowing that with Wanda gone it is her best shot at being able to break the spell on her Mama. A town over from Westview, in Easview Billy Maximoff, who is now inhabiting the body of William Kaplan, not that he realises that, suddenly opens his eyes, feeling something he has never felt before, the call of magic. As he feels the call of someone reaching out to him through his magic, Billy’s eyes glow purple, and he knows exactly what he has to do in the morning, even if he doesn’t understand why.

    Chapter 44

    Chapter 44 AN: Thank you so much for the support. As I have to go into the office Monday the next chapter will be out in about 14 hours. Then I will update the next chapter around 12 hours after that then about 20 hours after that will be the next chapter. Sorry about the cliffhanger for this chapter, hope you like it.

    As soon as she finished the spell, knowing deep inside of her that it worked, Prue makes her way back to her room, and climbs back into her bed without Nicky even realising that she was gone. While she misses her mom Prue is pretty sure that it is probably a good thing that her mother is off doing her job considering everything that Prue hopes to achieve.

    While she had breakfast with her brother and Lilia Prue quickly went outside and ever since has been sitting on the steps that lead to the door next to the garage, waiting. As he is feeling very curious about what is going on with his sister, and considering what she has been doing to herself feeling concerned, Nicky heads out of the front of the house and sits down next to her.

    “Do you want to talk to me about what is going on with you?” Nicky asks his sister, as he knows that something is going on with her. “I cast a spell last night,” Prue reveals, knowing that there is no point lying to her brother.

    “Okay,” Nicky says, suspecting it must be a big deal for Prue to say it like that. “What did the spell do?” Nicky asks confused.

    “Use my magic to reach out to Billy Maximoff’s magic, and make it so he will come to me,” Prue explains, making it seem like it is no big deal. “His soul and magic resurrected into a new body, he may not know who we are,” Nicky tells his sister.

    “Huh, I did not know that,” Prue admits, sounding surprised. “Then how did you know he was out there?” Nicky asks curious, as he knows that his sister would need to have known that Billy was out there to reach out to his magic.

    “I just felt his magic,” Prue explains. “I just assumed his body had been re- formed, but if he reincarnated into a new body that makes more sense,” Prue tells her brother as she knows that Billy’s body was created from chaos magic which that was intertwined with a reality Wanda reversed. “It does, but it may make it more difficult to have him understand who we are, what we need to do, and why,” Nicky tells his sister. “True,” Prue responds, and the two of them drift into silence as they sit together.

    For a little while Nicky and Prue sit in silence and wait until they see a boy who looks to be a little older than them ride a bike towards them. As they both sense something familiar about him Nicky and Prue both stand up as the boy gets off his bike at the end of the driveway and walks towards them. “Billy?” Prue asks, as she is sure about who he is, and she also realises something very interesting the closer she gets to him.

    “No, I am….,” Billy starts to say, but as he says what is obviously his name what Prue and Nicky realise is a sigil blocks his mouth, as that is something Agatha taught them about a long time ago, making it impossible for him to say his name. “Who are you? Why did I come here?” Billy asks, clearly looking confused, and as he does Nicky realises that he is holding something, and he suspects he knows exactly what that is. “Can you please trust me for a moment? And hand me what you are holding?” Nicky asks, as he realises that Billy is holding what looks to be a woodchip, with writing on it, but he knows is so much more, and for a moment Billy looks like he is considering something, but the reality he is trying to read Nicky and Prue’s minds, but he finds it impossible to do so, something which is both surprising to him, but incredibly confusing as for a year, from his perspective, he has been able to read anyone’s mind. “Okay,” Billy finally says, and he hands Nicky the object, which is actually a sigil and once he has it Nicky destroys it, and after he destroyed it Billy’s eyes glow for a second.

    “Has that helped you?” Nicky asks, once Billy’s eyes stop glowing, assuming that is the case.

    “I… yes,” Billy confirms, though he is still feeling very confused. “I am currently William Kaplan, at least that who this body once belonged to, but I was once Billy Maximoff,” Billy realises, as a lot, if not all, of his memories of his time in Westview come back to him. “Tommy,” Billy says, sounding heartbroken, then he realises who he is standing before him. “Nicky? Prue?” Billy asks, as he looks between them, recognizing them. “Yep,” Prue confirms. “Welcome back, Billy,” Prue says, smiling at him, feeling glad that her spell has worked in the way she intended, and also feeling glad she and Nicky have their friend back.

    “You cast a spell, brought me here,” Nicky realises, looking at Prue, knowing it was her without anyone saying so.

    “I did, because I need your help,” Prue tells him, feeling that there is no need to beat around the bush. “Your mother cast a spell on my mama, I need you to reverse it,” Prue tells Billy, who is feeling a little overwhelmed by all the information he has received in such a short amount of time. “Your mama?” Billy asks confused, having no idea who that is. “Agatha Harkness, but you knew her as Agnes,” Nicky explains, and for a moment Billy looks like he is trying to make sense of what he is being told. “I remember, she fought my…. Wanda,” Billy says, having no idea what else to call her as right now he has conflicting memories. “But she was really nice to me and Tommy, did her best to keep us away from the fight,” Billy remembers, remembering that well, now that he is focusing on that time.

    “So, you will help us?” Prue asks, feeing hope, as everything Billy just said made her think that he would be wiling to help his mother. “Yes,” Billy confirms. “But only if you help me find Tommy… I need my brother,” Billy says, knowing that the twins standing before him will understand that, more than anyone else in the universe.

    “Tommy is not currently in a body,” Nicky reveals.

    “Then where is he?” Billy asks concerned, having no idea how he knows that, but trusting that what Nicky is saying is the truth. “His soul is currently tied to you, between life and death, but not a ghost,” Prue explains to Billy, knowing that because she can feel Tommy’s power, even if his power isn’t witchcraft his speedster ability is a kind of power, of magic, which is why she can sense it.

    “He needs a body of his own,” Nicky tells Billy.

    “How does that happen?” Billy asks confused, as he doesn’t know exactly how he got a new body for himself, let alone how he is going to help Tommy get into a body, and Nicky and Prue exchange looks, an understanding passing between them.

    “We are going to have to work together,” Nicky reveals, knowing exactly what needs to happen next. “Prue can sense Tommy’s soul, you and I can direct him to a body of a person who is dying so he gets to it just as the person dies, you can resurrect him, and then, because we will be working together, Prue can heal any injury that the body has,” Nicky explains. “That’s really something we can do?” Billy asks amazed, looking between the twins.

    “Because the three of us are who we are, we can, but we have to be quick, before someone tries to stop us,” Prue tells Billy, knowing that there are going to be consequences from what they are doing, but if it gets her mother back she doesn’t care. “So, I am asking you to swear, right now, that once we get Tommy into a body, you will break the spell on Mama; no matter what,” Prue says to Billy as while she is wiling to help Billy, knowing that there will be extreme consequences including her mother’s anger, she is not going to do that if it doesn’t return her Mama to her.

    “I swear,” Billy says, sticking out his hand for Prue to shake, which she returns, both of them making an agreement that they will not break. “If we want to do this without being caught, we have to be quick, and we should go out back,” Nicky says, and the three of them start to head to the back yard.

    “I cannot explain why, but I think to break the spell on your mama we should work together, just like with Tommy,” Billy explains. “That would make sense,” Nicky says, suspecting that Billy can break the magic Wanda cast, Prue can reach out to their mothers’ magic, and he can help bring forth memories of their past.

    “Okay, where do we want to do this?” Billy asks, once they are outside. “Sit in a circle,” Prue says, and the three of them walk over to the middle of the backyard and sit down in a circle together. “We take hands,” Prue says, and the three of them doing exactly that. “We all need to close our eyes,” Prue says, and both Nicky and Billy listen to her, and do exactly that. “Our intentions need to be aligned, the only way we are going to do this is if the three of us work as one,” Prue explains to Billy and Nicky. “Billy, focus on Tommy, how much you love him, how much you want to be with him again, I have connected us to his soul,” Prue says. “Nicky,” Prue says, knowing her brother has to do the next part.

    “I feel him,” Nicky says. “Okay, Billy, it’s me and you,” Nicky says to him. “One hundred and twenty people die every minute, we just need to direct Tommy to the right one,” Nicky explains, knowing that is important. “The right one is whoever we can,” Billy says.

    “It is more complicated than that,” Prue tells him, as even if she isn’t a divination witch, she knows that.

    “I can feel it, where Tommy is meant to go,” Nicky tells his sister, knowing that not because of his divination ability but because of the magic he inherited from Rio. “Okay, a kid, about to be pushed through the ice, not far from here, same age as you Billy, he needs you, needs us, because he has no one else,” Nicky says, being able to feel that. “Now, you’re up Billy, focus on how much you want Tommy to be alive, how much you want him to have a second chance, how much you need your twin, your other half, to be back with you,” Nicky explains to Billy, clearly thinking about Prue when he talks about the connection Twins share. “Can you do that?” Nicky asks. “Yeah, I can,” Billy responds, knowing that he will do whatever he has to do to get his brother back.

    “Good. Prue, you know what you have to do when it is the right time,” Nicky tells Prue, who nods as she knows that while Billy can resurrect Tommy, she needs to heal him. “Okay Billy, let’s focus, we all know what we have to do,” Nicky says.

    Over the next few minutes Nicky, Prue, and Billy work together to resurrect Tommy, and once he is in a body Prue, using the connection the three of them have formed, is able to heal Tommy so that he is okay. “Billy, tell Tommy to hold onto what he is feeling to us for a moment longer, and I can unlock his powers so he can come to us,” Prue tells Billy, having had no idea that she could do that until this moment, but as she feels it, feels the magic connection of her, Billy, and Nicky, she knows without a doubt, that she can unlock the power inside of Tommy’s soul, which will allow him to become a speedster again, and come to them himself, rather than them needing to go looking for him.

    “Tommy, calm down, it is okay, you’re okay, we are going to help you,” Billy promises, while he cannot feel what Prue is feeling, he does know that the magic of the three of them is connected, and because of that he is pretty sure that there is nothing they can’t do. “Prue, if you speak, I think I can channel your words through to Tommy, so that he can hear you say what you need to say,” Billly says, and even though she knows Tommy won’t see because all their eyes are closed, but she nods.

    “Tommy, it is me, Prue. I can help you, take a few deep breaths for me,” Prue requests, as Billy makes it possible for Tommy to hear her words. “Feel deep inside of you, the power inside of you, building, getting stronger, coming to the surface, needing to be expelled…. Run Tommy, run,” Prue says to him.

    “Come to us, you can find us, we will look after you,” Nicky says, Billy making it possible so that Tommy can hear her words too, and for a few moments the three of them wait.

    “Billy,” A voice says causing Nicky, Prue, and Billy to open their eyes, and they see, standing before them, a young boy, with light brown, longer hair, who looks to be the same age as Billy, standing before them, it being clear to the trio that he used his superspeed to run to them.

    “Tommy,” Billy says, and he quickly let’s go of Nicky and Prue’s hand, and runs towards his brother, who he embraced.

    “Billy? It’s really you?” Tommy asks, feeling shocked.

    “Yeah, it’s me, I’ve got you,” Billy promises his brother as the two of them hug.

    As the Maximoff Twins hug each other both Nicky and Prue also stand up, and hug each other, both feeling incredible proud that they managed to reunite another set of twins.

    “What is gong on out here?” Lilia asks, as she walks outside, as while she cannot sense magic in the same way Prue, or even Agatha, can, even she knows enough to know that some powerful magic just occurred, and she isn’t surprised, even if she should be, to realise it was Prue and Nicky who did it.

    “A lot,” Prue answers. “Zietta, meet Billy and Tommy Maximoff,” Prue introduces, as Billy and Tommy break apart. “Billy, Tommy, this is Lilia Calderu, our aunt,” Prue introduces, and while Lilia is thrilled to be introduced as that, she is extremely, concerned, and confused, about everything that is going on.

    “I know you… kind of, or William did. I’m still making sense of everything,” Billy admits, seeing Lilia, and knowing that the body he is in has met her, even if he technically hasn’t.

    “I saw what was going to happen to you, but I didn’t see this,” Lilia admits, feeling incredibly confused, and realising that the Sigil she put in place must have been destroyed.

    “I am so sorry, Zietta,” Agatha mutters as she continues to watch the memory that is playing out before her.

    “Family,” Lilia answered as she put her arm around Rio’s shoulders. “Who are Nicky and Prue?” Agnes asked.

    “Everything to you!” Agatha exclaims, hating that she put the people she loves most through situations like this many times.

    “Rio, we should go,” Lilia said. “Agnes is not who you’re mad at,” Lilia says.

    “No, I am, and she should be,” Agatha says, guilt in her voice, as she can see how much pian she is causing Rio in the memory and she hates that fact.

    “No, it’s not,” Rio said. “I’m sorry, Agnes,” Rio said and as Lilia lead her out of the memory Agatha is throw back out of the memory and back to reality.

    “Agatha? Are you okay?” Rio asks concerned, when she realises that Agatha has come out of the memory.

    “No,” Agatha admits. “We need to talk,” Agatha says to Rio, pulling her hand away from Rio, which feels Rio with dread about what Agatha has just seen, and she stands up.

    “Agatha we really don’t have time for this,” Jen tells her, as Prue and Nicky exchange looks, both feeling confused, and concerned, about what their mother just saw.

    “We’re making time,” Agatha says, looking at Jen, there being no room for arguing in her voice, before turning to her daughter. “Prue, I need you to join us,” Agatha tells her daughter, telling her, Rio, Nicky, and Lilia what Agatha’s memory was likely connected to.

    “Okay Mama,” Prue says and both she and Rio get up and follow Agatha, the three of them walking away until they are a little way away from the others, and once she is sure that they won’t be overheard Agatha turns to Prue and Rio.

    “Mama?” Prue asks hesitantly, being able to see the pain in her mothers’ eyes. “Did you see something bad?” Prue asks worried, feeling worried about her mama.

    “I saw a glimpse of the pain I caused by being under the spell,” Agatha admits. “Prue, Sweetheart, have you been hurting yourself?” Agatha asks her daughter, having no idea how else to ask the question, other than just asking it outright.

    “Yes,” Prue asks, the simple word breaking Agatha’s heart. “But I have been healing myself every time I do, and I have not been trying to kill myself, I promise, Mama, I just needed to feel in control,” Prue tells her mama, speaking quickly, telling her the same thing she told her mom when Rio found out.

    Hearing her daughters’ words, and remembering feeling a lot like that, Agatha moves forward and hugs her, holding her close, reminding herself that despite everything Prue is still with her; that she has a chance to help her in a way no one helped her when she was Prue’s age.

    “It is okay to feel like that,” Agatha assures her daughter. “But it is not okay to hurt yourself. It doesn’t help, not really, trust me, I’ve been there,” Agatha tells her daughter.

    “You have?” Prue asks, looking at her, feeling surprised.

    “I have,” Agatha confirms, and as she watches the understanding pass between her wife and daughter Rio knows that this is what she always knew Prue needed, to talk to Agatha about this because Agatha truly understands. “Sweetheart, I know what it feels like to feel like you are in control of nothing, to be in so much pain and have no physical representation of it that you feel the need to create one, but I also know that as much as it helps in the moment, or even for a few seconds later, that feeling of relief, or help, doesn’t last,” Agatha tells her daughter, wanting her to understand that as she wants her to be on a better path than her.

    “It does not?” Prue asks, looking worried about that.

    “No, it doesn’t,” Agatha tells her daughter. “Which is why we need to find a different way to help you to feel in control, and we will, I promise we will,” Agatha promises. “Prue, you need to know that not all pain needs a physical representation,” Agatha tells her daughter. “Sometimes the pain we’re in leaves scars that can’t be seen, and that doesn’t make it any less valid,” Agatha tells her daughter, giving an understanding that Rio as a cosmic being is unable to give.

    “I… I have never thought of it like that,” Prue admits, looking like she is considering her mothers words.

    “That’s okay,” Agatha tells her daughter, before hugging her again. “You are not alone, Prue, you don’t have to experience what you are feeling alone,” Agatha tells her daughter, knowing that she will not let her daughter go through this alone.

    “So, Mom’s said,” Prue says, as she feels her mother kiss the top of her head, and after a few more moments the two of them break apart. “Prue and I have a deal,” Rio reveals, and Agatha looks at her. “I have put a charm on the knife Prue uses to hurt herself so I know if she uses it, but she will also tell me if she does hurt herself,” Rio tells Agatha. “I’ve promised Prue that I will always do my best to be honest with her, and she will always do her best to be honest with me, us, too,” Rio explains. “That sounds like a fair deal,” Agatha says, feeling that that could also help Prue to feel in control. “Prue, I want you to know that you can always be honest with me too,” Agatha tells her daughter.

    “I will remember that,” Prue assures her mother, and for a few moments things seem to be tense, but Prue knows it is not directed at her. “Would you like me to give you a moment alone?” Prue asks her parents. “That would be good, Sweet Girl,” Rio tells her, and hearing that Prue nods and walks over to the others, and once she is out of hearing range Rio turns to Agatha. “You remembered when I yelled at you, didn’t you?” Rio asks, and the look on Agatha’s face is more than enough to confirm what she is thinking. “Agatha I’m sorry…”Rio starts to say, but Agatha cuts her off, turning to look at her.

    “Don’t, you have no reason to apologise,” Agatha assures her wife. “You were hurting, you found out our daughter was hurting herself, your reaction was understandable,” Agatha assures her. “I don’t blame you, at all,” Agatha assures her.

    “I blame me,” Rio reveals. “Prue had been hurting herself for months when I caught her, and I didn’t even realise,” Rio reveals.

    “If she was healing herself you couldn’t have,” Agatha tells her. “How long has it been since she hurt herself?” Agatha asks, needing to know so that she knows how to help Prue.

    “About two weeks,” Rio tells Agatha. “But she told me, and she has also been telling me when she has thought about herself but then hasn’t,” Rio says, feeling that it is important to tell Agatha that. “I am sorry I didn’t tell you the moment the spell broke, but…” Rio starts to say.

    “It’s okay, there wasn’t a good time,” Agatha assures her before hugging her wife. “We’ll figure it out, we’ll help her,” Agatha promises, making it clear that Rio no longer has to carry the weight of this alone.

    “We have to,” Rio responds, and the two of them continue to stand together, holding one another, both feeling unbelievable sadness for their little girl, and knowing that they have to do everything they can to help her, to help her truly understand that hurting herself isn’t the answer.

    “That is a good idea,” Agatha says, and she, Rio, Nicky, and Prue walk over to where, near the largest of the four tents, there are some log seats so that they can talk privately and as they do that Alice and Jen sit together, as do Billy, and Tommy, and finally Lilia and Sharon also sit together; all ten of them spreading out throughout the campsite that has been set up for them. “Are you both okay after everything you’ve seen and heard?” Rio asks her children concerned, as the three of them, and Agatha, sit down together, Rio knowing that they have already been struggling with all the adjustments they have already experienced and now they have even more adjustments thrown at them.

    “I think so,” Nicky admits, and Prue nods. “Are you okay, Mama?” Nicky asks curious, clearly worried about his mother; something which he has spent most of the last year doing.

    “I… I think so,” Agatha says, only being so close to being ‘honest’ because it is her children she is talking to, and even If it is difficult for her, she long ago decided that she will do her best not to lie to them. “I am so sorry that I don’t remember the last year, that I don’t remember what we did together, and I am sorry that you had to experience a version of me forgetting you every few days,” Agatha tells her children, having no idea how much that would have hurt them, but hating herself a little because of that as if the memory of Rio she saw was any indication it was very difficult for the people who love her to experience.

    “Mama, it is okay,” Prue assures her. “We always knew it was not your fault,” Prue assures her.

    “I appreciate you saying that,” Agatha tells her children, which tells Rio she still blames herself, despite their children’s words, which means there is a conversation they have to have when it is just the two of them, as she wants to protect Prue and Nicky from the guilt they are feeling. “I know the last year must have been a lot,” Agatha says, having no idea just how write she is. “How are you both handling being in the twenty first century?” Agatha asks her children, assuming that is a big adjustment, wanting to know more about them, while also wanting to get attention of her.

    “It is a lot,” Nicky admits. “It is overwhelming, it feels like every day I am experiencing something that is different, some of it is good, but everything, food especially, is strange,” Nicky admits, and Rio is a little amused he mentioned how much he is struggling with different food as has seen that first hand.

    “Nothing feels familiar other than the three of you, and Señor Scratchy,” Prue admits. “Zietta said that as witches we experience the world differently, but even knowing that it has been hard experiencing what feels like a completely new world,” Prue admits.

    “Zietta is right, as witches we do experience the world differently,” Agatha assures her children, feeling incredibly glad that her aunt has been helping her children, especially considering she couldn’t. “But what you two should remember is that in an instant you travelled over two hundred and fifty years into the future. I have experienced the changes in this world as they occurred and I still struggle with them. So, finding nothing familiar, finding it overwhelming is completely understandable,” Agatha assures her children, who are comforted by her words. “When we finish the road we can slowly figure out what you are both comfortable with, and slowly start to do new things, how does that sound?” Agatha asks her children, assuming that Lilia and Rio have tried to help, but both of them tend to keep themselves a little removed from the world, so it is not surprising that this is something that they would be struggling to help the kids with. “That sounds good,” Prue says, and Nicky nods in agreement, though both of them are also feeling a little nervous.

    “Nicky, Prue, do you want to tell Mama all the things you’ve learnt about your magic since you’ve been in the twenty first century?” Rio asks her children, knowing that that is something that will mean a lot to all three of them, and it has the upside of being something that will distract them all from the things they are feeling guilty about.

    “Definitely,” Prue says excitedly, and she proceeds to tell her mother things she has learnt, things she has realised, while Nicky also talks about things, he has learnt he has some difficulty to get a word in as his sister is so excited to talk about magic, but more than that Nicky realises she is excited to talk about magic with their mama.

    Across the campsite from where Agatha, Rio, Prue, and Nicky are talking Alice and Jen are sitting together, both of them thinking about what they saw when they relived their memoires.

    “So, you know Agatha and Rio?” Alice asks, deciding to actually talk to Jen rather than getting caught up in her memories of her mother, as considering everything she feels like it would be best.

    “For a little over two hundred years…. Agatha a little longer than Rio,” Jen explains, looking very much like she doesn’t want to talk about this, something which Alice realises but decides to ignore, as with everything Jen says, or rather doesn’t say, she finds herself becoming more curious. “And you’re… Friends?” Alice asks, sounding almost hesitant, but she wants to know more about what the history between the trio is, as she is sure that it will become very relevant at some point, and Jen gives a bitter laugh.

    “I would use a lot of words to describe us, friends is not the first one that comes to mind,” Jen comments, knowing there was a time when that was very different.

    “So, what is the first word that comes to mind?” Alice asks curious. “Complicated,” Jen answers, and because she really doesn’t want to talk about her history with Agatha and Rio, she decides to ask something she is curious about. “So, your mom made the Ballard popular, was she trying to get here?” Jen asks, as that is what it seems like to her, and if Alice is going to ask her uncomfortable questions, she is going to ask uncomfortable questions back.

    “Yes,” Alice says. “As long as I can remember she kept trying to open the road… I guess it wasn’t the right time, or coven,” Alice realises. “She would be amazed to see all this,” Alice admits, as she looks around. “It is pretty amazing,” Jen admits, as even she can acknowledge that, and then she realises something. “Wait, as long as you can remember, were you actually born in the 1980s?” Jen asks wanting to clarify that as she knows when Lorna was born.

    “Um, yeah,” Alice says, sounding confused about why that is such a big deal.

    “You are a child!” Jen says shocked, knowing that while Prue, Nicky, Billy and Tommy are actual children in comparison to how old the rest of them is Alice is basically a child to them too.

    “I’m really not,” Alice says annoyed. “Wait, how old are you?” Alice asks. “Oh Alice, you never ask a witch that question… unless your Agatha,” Jen says, causing the two of them to laugh, and Jen feels the kind of inner peace she hasn’t felt for a long time, even with her health care range. “Glad they are getting along,” Sharon notes as she and Lilia sit together, a little way away from where Alice and Jen are sitting.

    “It is good to see,” Lilia admits, suspecting that it might be one of the few times where there is actual laughter on the Road. “How are you doing with everything?” Lilia asks curious.

    “I’m… I’m not sure,” Sharon admits. “After what Wanda did, I knew magic was real, but the truth is I have tried very hard to forget about it,” Sharon admits, as after the spell broke it was easier to forget about it. “That’s understandable, from what I know it was painful to be under her control,” Lilia says as from what has been explained over the last year that is what she has realised.

    “It was,” Sharon admits. “But since Todd died, I understand what she did, if I could bring him back…” Sharon starts to say, but then she trails off as she isn’t sure if it would be awful to admit what she is feeling. “You would,” Lilia finishes, and Sharon nods. “That’s understandable,” Lilia assures her.

    “Have you ever been married?” Sharon asks curious.

    “No… I have mostly spent my years alone,” Lilia admits, as while she has had relationships over the centuries every single time, she has lot the person she was with and was reminded why it was better being alone. “That sounds lonely,” Sharon admits, frowning slightly.

    “It can be,” Lilia admits.

    “Well, that’s not good, no one should be alone,” Sharon tells Lilia. “If you believe that then why have you been shutting yourself off since Todd died?” Lilia asks, having been enough to realise that. “Because I don’t know what else to do,” Sharon admits. “We were married for forty years, I don’t know what my life looks like without him,” Sharon says sadly, as she never thought she would have to figure it out. “No one does when everything familiar is suddenly gone,” Lilia admits, thinking about all the life altering moments she has experienced over the centuries.

    “How do you go on?” Sharon asks, getting the impression that Lilia has experienced loosing everything multiple times before.

    “You just do,” Lilia says, having no other explanation. “You find something, even if it’s just something as simple as wanting to see another sunrise or try a different recipe or see a flower bloom, and let that help you keep going, eventually you’ll realise you have built a new life,” Lilia says. “It won’t be the same, and at times it will still be painful, but it will be enough,” Lilia explains. “Sharon, you are apart of a coven now, you’re not alone. You don’t have to figure out your new life alone,” Lilia tells her, knowing that before now she and Sharon haven’t been particular close, even if she has admired the way she has looked out for Nicky and Prue, but now Lilia feels responsible for her.

    “I… thank you,” Sharon says amazed, and the two of them drift into silence.

    Not far from where Lilia and Sharon are talking Billy and Tommy are also sitting together, and while Billy realised that he was comforted by what he saw in his memory he knows that Tommy is feeling the opposite. “Are you okay?” Billy asks his brother, who has ben uncharacteristically quite for a while.

    “I’m not sure,” Tommy admits.

    “Do you want to talk about what you experienced?” Billy asks his brother. “No, it wasn’t my memory, not really,” Tommy tells his brother. “But you still experienced it, it felt like it was,” Billy points out. “That had to have an effect on you,” Billy says concerned.

    “It… he was in so much pain,” Tommy admits. “No one loved him, no one cared, all he knew was hurt… I felt that, felt what he felt,” Tommy says, and Billy can hear the pain in his brother’s voice.

    “You know that is not true for you, right?” Billy asks his brother, needing his brother to know that. “You are loved, you are not alone, even if we don’t have mom and dad right now you have me, just like I have you,” Billy tells his brother, remembering what his mom once told them.

    “I know,” Tommy assures him. “But you know what I think we don’t only have each other, even without mom and dad,” Tommy admits, as he looks around at all the people they have with them.

    “I think you’re right,” Billy admits, and as he does Prue and Nicky walk over and join them. “Hey,” Billy greats as the Vidal-Harkness twins join him and Tommy.

    “Hey,” Nicky says. “We wanted to check how you two are doing,” Nicky admits.

    “Considering everything I’d say we’re doing okay,” Tommy admits. “How about the two of you?” Tommy asks curious.

    “I would say we are feeling the same,” Prue admits. “Though honestly this place feels more familiar, more comfortable, than anywhere else I have been in a year,” Prue reveals, as while she may not be a green witch she is perfectly comfortable within a forest.

    “That is so strange,” Billy says, having no idea what to think about that, but knowing he is curious.

    “True though,” Prue says amused, and the four twins laugh as they sit together.

    Not far from where the two sets of twins are sitting together and talking Rio and Agatha are far enough away that they cannot hear what the foursome are talking about, but close enough to be able to tell how happy they are. “Have they made friends in Westview?” Agatha asks, as she moves so that she is leaning against Rio.

    “No,” Rio says, as she moves her arms so that she can wrap them around Agatha. “I think they both feel like they won’t be able to relate to anyone, so they haven’t tried,” Rio admits. “We talked about the two of them going to school, I thought it could help them get used to the new time, but they didn’t like the idea,” Rio admits.

    “It might have felt like too big of an adjustment to them,” Agatha realises. “That it was just something else that was different that was going to be forced on them,” Agatha says, understanding that.

    “That’s what I think,” Rio admits. “But I still think it could be good for them, it would at least give them a chance to make some friends,” Rio tells Agatha.

    “Looks like they’ve already made friends,” Agatha notes, as she watches Nicky, Prue, Billy, and Tommy together.

    “Yeah, they have,” Rio confirms. “They were friends when Wanda had her hex up,” Rio reveals.

    “They were?” Agatha asks surprised, and Rio nods. “Were Nicky and Prue effected by the hex?” Agatha asks.

    “No,” Rio answers, before deciding to fill Agatha in on a few things. “When Nicky and Prue got to 2023, they appeared in the middle of a Road, Sharon found them and took them to hospital,” Rio explains, and Agatha finds herself feeling incredibly grateful for Sharon. “For eighteen days Nicky received treatments and Prue stayed close,” Rio explains. “When he was medically cleared Sharon invited them to stay with her until we were found, which is what they did,” Rio explains. “They arrived in Westview just as Wanda cast her spell, Prue felt it come into existence, but they were unaffected by it,” Rio explains. “They decided to investigate what was going on,”

    “Of course they did,” Agatha says, a little amused by that, and then she realises something. “A week, we were so close to them for a week and didn’t realise,” Agatha says, guilt in her voice.

    “I know. When I realised, I couldn’t believe it either,” Rio says, guilt in her voice. “It was thanks to Billy I found out,” Rio says, and Agatha gives her a curious look. “When you were making food, he told me that I reminded him of his friends Prue and Nicky,” Rio explains.

    “Which is why you ran out,” Agatha realises.

    “I’m sorry I didn’t tell you,” Rio says. “I should have, i…” Rio starts to say. “It’s okay,” Agatha assures her. “You didn’t know what Wanda was going to do,” Agatha tells Rio.

    “I still feel guilty, we lost a year together,” Rio says, hating that. “We did, but we’ll make up for it,” Agatha says, feeling determined to do that. “But um, it might be six of us rather than just four,” Agatha realises, as she knows she cannot turn her back of Billy and Tommy, that she will be whatever they need her to be, she just hopes Rio is okay with that. “Seven,” Rio corrects, and for a second Agatha is confused, until Rio gestures to over where Lilia is sitting.

    “Right, seven,” Agatha says amused. “I am glad Lilia has been able to help,” Agatha admits.

    “She did more than just help, I don’t know if we would have been able to get through the last year without her,” Rio admits, feeling that it is important she mentions that.

    “Then I am even gladder for her,” Agatha admits, knowing that she wants to talk to her aunt when she gets a chance but right now, she doesn’t want to move out of Rio’s arms. “So, the two of us, a, almost four hundred- and fifty-year-old divination witch aunt, and four incredibly powerful children who are capable of breaking the universe on a whim, that’s our family?” Agatha asks, knowing that that is incredibly unconventional, but also feels incredibly right.

    “Yep, and a rabbit,” Rio adds, smiling at that.

    “Of course, can’t forget Señor Scratchy,” Agatha says amused, as the two of them drift into a comfortable silence as they continue to sit together, watching everyone else, both realising that Nicky and Prue seem relaxed which means everything to them.

For a couple of minutes, the coven walks until they finally see, in the distant, what appears to be a Hamptons style house.

Getting to the porch, it is clear that no one wants to be the one to enter first, until Agatha, realising that no one else is going to, reaches out and opens the door, walking in and causing the others to follow behind. Just like when they entered the last trial as soon as the group enter, they find that their clothes and hair have been changed to fit the environment, which in this case is that of upper-class people on a Hamptons vacation. “Why is everything so white?” Prue asks, looking down at the outfit she has been put in, while her long hair has been put up into a uncomfortably high ponytail.

Agatha on the other hand walks over to her wife.

    “But you still shared something with her that you didn’t share with me,” Rio reminds Agatha. “She was there for you when it was too painful for us to be together,” Rio says, feeling torn between being thankful for being happy that Jen was there for Agatha and being jealous and angry for the same reason.

    “She was, but I would have rather been with you,” Agatha assures her wife before leaning forward and kissing her wife.

My tricks are well-known,” Prue reads. “A riddle,” Agatha realises. “Sounds like a witch,” Agatha comments. “Sounds like you,” Jen tells Agatha, who rolls her eyes, and as she does Sharon turns and sees something on the table.

Ten points to Sharon!” Alice says, sounding impressed, and they all turn to look at the table where there is the wine, glasses, and a timer. “So, this is worryingly obvious, we need to drink the wine,” Alice realises. “I’m sure that the trial will actually start once we drink it,” Agatha assumes. “Would make sense,” Rio realises, as Jen picks up the bottle to have a look at it.

    “To good health, ¡Salud!,” Agatha says, and while the others, with the exception of Rio, take a drink, the timer starting the second the first person takes a drink, Agatha hesitates.

    “How about we move the girl talk over to the couch,” Sharon suggests, and as they others nod, they head over to the couch, leaving Prue and Tommy by the table. As the others, including Nicky and Tommy, walk over to the couch Prue gives a slight nod to Tommy, who uses his powers to run to the kitchen and get two more cups, that look different from the glasses the others are using, without anyone seeing.

    Once Tommy is back to Prue’s side Prue pours a small bit of wine into each cup, the others being so caught up in their own conversations that they don’t realise, and once Prue pours the drinks both she and Tommy pick them up and silently toast each other, both of them smirking as they feel proud about what they have managed to do without anyone else noticing. “So, witches are just another name for a bad girl, is that right?” Sharon asks, trying to make sense of everything, having already finished her single glass of wine.

Any brooms? No sir?” Lilia, who finishes the last of her wine, says, clearly annoyed, and as she says that Agatha, who finishes her wine too, notices that Prue and Tommy are still over by the wine, and are holding cups.

    “Prudence, Thomas, please tell me you did not just do what I think you just did,” Agatha says to the pair, causing everyone to look at them, it being perfectly clear that she is worried about the two of them. “We did not do what you think we did,” Prue and Tommy say together, both lying, which everyone realises.

    “You shouldn’t have done that,” Rio tells the two of them, having an awful feeling about what is going to happen.

    “Okay, we have to work out what the toxin is, so because of that I am going to ask you some questions,” Jen says, walking over to Sharon, while Prue and Tommy walk over to the rest of the group. “Do you feel a tingling in the back of your throat?” Jen asks.

    “No,”

    “Do you taste mulberries?” Jen asks.

    “What do mulberries taste like?” Sharon asks confused.

    “Do you hear any ringing or the sound of fairies crying?” Jen asks, ignoring the question, and Sharon looks confused.

    “The swelling is disappearing,” Billy realises.

    “No, that is very not good,” Jen says, knowing how bad that is. “The fact that the symptoms are progressing so quickly means it can only be one thing, Alewife’s Revenge,” Jen explains.

    “And how bad is that?” Agatha asks, looking worriedly at Prue and Tommy. “Bad, it causes facial swelling, dizziness, delirium, hallucinations, loss of motor function, and, if not treated in time, death,” Jen explains. “Antidote?” Prue asks, already feeling herself starting to overheat. “Yes, um, we need gut of a eusocial instinct, frankincense, eye of newt, corpse of something that has been decaying for thirty million years,” Jen recites.

    “Let’s split up and get everything we need,” Lilia suggests. “We’ll meet in the kitchen,” Jen says, and she turns to Sharon. “Can you find something in the kitchen that we could put the antidote in? It would have to be big and be able to be boiled,” Jen tells her, as she knows they are meant to do this trial together.

    “Sure, I can do that,” Sharon says, before heading to the kitchen. “Everyone else split up and get what we need,” Jen instructs. “Prue, Tommy, you’re with Mama and I,” Rio tells the pair, both of them nod.

    “We meet back in the kitchen as soon as we have what we need,” Jen instructs, and everyone splits up, Prue and Tommy walking over to Rio and Agatha.

    “Once we are done with this task, we are going to have a conversation about how reckless you both were,” Agatha says, looking between Prue and Tommy, sounding annoyed, but she is actually worried about them. “Yes Mama,” Prue says.

    “If you experience any of the symptoms you tell us immediately,” Rio tells the pair, both of whom nod. “Good, let’s go,” Rio says, and just like everyone else they start to search the house for what they need. About five minutes after the ten people on the witches road split up they have all collected the ingredients they need, and have made their way back to the kitchen where Sharon has filled the sink with water and also collected a device that will make it possible to boil the potion when it is time. “We are running out of time,” Nicky says worried, feeling terrified that someone is going to die, that they are not going to be able to get the antidote created in time, as he has witnessed so many of the others experiencing horrible hallucinations.

    “That’s why we have to move quickly,” Jen tells him. “Okay, the elements need to be added in a certain order, in a specific time, starting with guts and eye,” Jen says and once she does Sharon adds the eye of newt while Rio adds the honey.

    “Next is frankincense?” Alice says as she goes to add it, but Jen knocks her hand out of the way.

    “Noi, no, no wait, get outta here,” Jen says to her. “Where’s the zooplankton?” Jen asks, and Agatha shows her what she and Rio collected, bottles and containers of Jen’s skin care range.

    “Now we need to stir the potion,” Jen says, and Sharon is able to pick up a wooden spoon. “With your dominate hand, counter clockwise,” Jen says as Rio notices Prue reach out and grab hold of the counter to remain standing, and Sharon does just that.

    “Everyone who drank potion pull a strand of hair outta your head now,” Jen instructs. “A single hair only, hurry up,” Jen instructs, and as she realises that Prue cannot lift her hand Agatha pulls out one of her daughters’ hairs and gives it to her.

    “It’s like a blue-green,” Nicky says, as he looks worriedly at his sister. “Maybe like a teal?” Nicky suggests.

    “It’s green, Nicky,” Lilia tells him.

    “Something is wrong,” Sharon says, worried.

    “I must have forgotten something,” Jen realises.

    “One minute left,” Alice realises, feeling terrified for Prue and Tommy who are seemingly more effected by the poison than the others. “What did you forget?” Agatha asks Jen.

    “I don’t know! I’ve never made this potion before!” Jen exclaims. “I make retinol serums, for Christ’s sake!” Jen exclaims.

    “There was a time where I would be able to solve this with a wave of my hand, but now? I’m bound,” Jen says, looking upset. “They stole my magic! we’re all going to die here!” Jen exclaims, moving away from the sink. “No, I don’t want to die here,” Jen says, starting to break down. “This is not where I die!” Jen exclaims, and after making sure that Rio has got both Prue and Tommy Agatha walks over to Jen and puts her hands on her shoulders. “I know you hate me, that you have spent the last two centuries avoiding me because you didn’t want to hear anything I had to say, but you need to listen to me right now,” Agatha tells Jen. “The work you do is important, and I am not talking about this Kale Kare crap,” Agatha tells Jen. “I’m talking about the real work, you can be that witch again, they can take your power, Jen, but they can’t take your knowledge,” Agatha tells her, and for a moment it looks like Jen is considering her words. “Jen,” Agatha says, her voice rushed.

    “Blood,” Jen realises.
