    “You’ve jinxed us,” Tommy tells him.

    “Crap,” Billy says worried.

    “We will figure it out, whatever comes next,” Nicky assures the others. “Prediction?” Billy asks curious.

    “Yeah… I think so, but I am not sure,” Nicky admits. “I just know that the four of us, our fates are intertwined, and we are going to continue to be very important to each other,” Nicky admits.

    “Good to know,” Prue admits, as she can tell that both Tommy and Billy are curious about that as well. “So, I know what Nicky and I have to adjust too, but the two of you have some intense adjustments too, how are you doing?” Prue asks curious.

    “I’m trying to get used to having two sets of memory, it’s hard, but remembering times with mom and dad have been helping with that,” Billy reveals.

    “That sounds like a good thing,” Prue says and Billy nods. “What about you, Tommy?” Prue asks curious.

    “I feel good,” Tommy admits. “The memories of Thomas Shepard are in the background, but I can push them down, I feel like me, I just…” Tommy starts to say.

    “Just what? Tommy?” Nicky asks in a gentle voice.

    “I miss my Mom, Wanda, I want her back,” Tommy admits. “Your mom confirmed she is dead, but also suspects she will find her way back to Billy and I,” Tommy explains. “I just hope it happens sooner rather than later,” Tommy admits.

    “That is understandable,” Nicky admits. “What about your Dad? Do you know what happened to him?” Nicky asks curious.

    “He stopped existing when Mom reversed her spell, just like us, but he didn’t reincarnate,” Billy explains, knowing that.

    “Sword created a version of him, that Dad fought, but I don’t know what that means,” Tommy admits.

    “Me either,” Billy admits.

    “We can help you figure it out, if you would like,” Prue offers, wanting to do something to help them.

    “Thank you, do you mind if I get back to you on that one?” Tommy asks. “Of course not, whenever you are ready, we are here, I promise,” Nicky assures them.

    “What he said,” Prue responds.

    “Thank you,” Billy and Tommy respond, and for a few moments the foursome sit in comfortable silence until Billy decides to ask something he is curious about.

    “Prue, how can you use your magic in both delicate, and strong ways? Like you can explode but you can also use your magic so specifically that you could move a cork out of a wine bottle without doing anything to the bottle, how did you do that?” Billy asks curious.

    “Practice,” Prue says, as she makes magic dance around her fingers, showing the three boys. “Magic is apart of you Billy, you just have to learn to embrace it, make it so using it feels as natural as breathing,” Prue explains.

    “Is that how it feels like for you?” Tommy asks curious.

    “Yep,” Prue confirms.

    “Wow,” Billy says amazed. “What else can you tell me about magic?” Billy asks.

    “Whatever you want to know,” Prue says, and while she and Billy proceed to talk about Magic Tommy talks to Nicky about all the amazing things about the twenty first century.

    In the tent next to the four kids are Agatha and Rio are lying next to each other, holding each other as they lay with one another for the first time in a year.

    “I can hear you thinking from here,” Rio says to her wife. “What is going on in that beautiful head of yours?” Rio asks, and Agatha smiles at the compliment.

    “I’m just thinking,” Agatha responds.

    “Anything you want to share?” Rio asks curious.

    “It is so strange to me it feels like I just yesterday I had no idea where Prue and Nicky were, that I had the Darkhold, that I was fighting Wanda… but now I know that was a year ago, and I am powerless,” Agatha reveals, and Rio can’t help but tense at the mention of the Darkhold.

    “Agatha, my love, you may not be able to access your magic right now, but I promise you that you are not powerless,” Rio assures her wife. “I love you,” Agatha tells her, feeling amazed by Rio, and truly feeling that she doesn’t deserve her incredible wife.

    “I love you to,” Rio responds. “Agatha, how does it feel for you not to have the Darkhold?” Rio asks worried, as she cannot help but worry about the lingering effects the Darkhold will have on Agatha.

    “Honestly…. It feels like a weight is gone,” Agatha admits. “I would have done whatever I had to do to save our kids, and I will do whatever they need, but the Darkhold being destroyed… I am not sure that is a bad thing,” Agatha admits.

    “Guess Wanda did something right,” Rio responds.

    “Did you fight her?” Agatha asks curious, as from what Rio told Billy and Tommy, she is sure that Wanda and Rio had some kind of confrontation. “Not exactly, I knocked her down a few times, we talked, and she jumped through the portal that took her on to where she was meant to be,” Rio explains. “Agatha, I am sorry that I couldn’t get her to reverse the spell,” Rio tells her wife.

    “It’s okay, Sweetheart, it is not your fault,” Agatha assures her wife. “It feels like it is, it feels like I should have done more,” Rio admits. “From what I have seen, and what Prue and Nicky have said, you have done everything you could, you’ve been amazing the last year, Baby,” Agatha tells her wife. “I am so proud of you, I love you so much,” Agatha assures her.

    “All I wanted was you back, to have our family back together,” Rio admits. “And that is exactly what has happened,” Agatha tells her. “We’re back together,” Agatha reminds her.

    “Yeah, we are,” Rio says, as she leans down and kisses Agatha’s head. “I am never letting go of you, or our kids, again,” Rio says. “Me either,” Agatha responds. “Rio how worried do we have to be about your sister?” Agatha asks concerned.

    “I honestly don’t know,” Rio admits. “I think if we successfully complete the Road, and Hecate gets involved we should be fine,” Rio admits. “Infinity cares to much about the Sacred Balance to do something once Hecate has her say,” Rio explains.

    “But what if we don’t complete the road, or if it takes too long to do so?” Agatha asks worried.

    “Then we might have a problem,” Rio admits. “But if it gets to that, Agatha, I promise I will not let Infinity hurt you, or our kids, no matter what it takes,” Rio says, and because she knows her wife so well Agatha knows the implication of what she is saying.

    “Let’s just hope it doesn’t get to that point,” Agatha says, as she knows she doesn’t want to risk loosing her wife because she sacrificed herself to protect their family from her sister.

    “Let’s,” Rio responds, and Agatha yawns. “Get some sleep, Mi Amore, I’ve got you,” Rio assures her.

    “The kids…” Agatha starts to object.

    “Are fine, I will check on them,” Rio assures Agatha. “I promise, I will keep you, and them safe, but you need rest,” Rio assures Agatha, starting to run her hand through Agatha’s hair as she can tell how tense Agatha is. “Okay,” Agatha responds, though she is clearly worried, and as she closes her eyes Rio continues to run her hand through her hair. Within minutes because Agatha feels so safe, so relaxed, in her wife’s arms Agatha falls asleep as Rio holds her while also listening for any signs of danger, or signs that tell her the kids aren’t okay.

    Chapter 55

    Chapter 55 AN: So, I am so busy right now that for a little longer I am only going to be able to update once a day for a little longer. I am so sorry about that. hopefully I will be able to increase updates again soon, but I also think I might be getting close to the end of the story so we’ll see how I go. A few hours after Rio, or at least that it is what it feels like to her, promised Agatha that she would keep everyone safe she hasn’t heard any noise from anything, or felt sensed anything that made her feel concerned, or at least was the case until she heard movement out in the campsite. “Sleep my love,” Rio says to Agatha, placing a gentle kiss on her wife’s temple before she careful moves Agatha off her and heads out of the tent, feeling curious about who it is that is awake.

    As soon as she walks out of the tent Rio very much regrets her decision to leave Agatha as out of the out eight other people who are on the road it is Jen who Rio finds looking around.

    “Oh, it’s you,” Jen says to Rio, having looked over when she heard the footsteps, and it is clear that she is less than happy to see Rio. “Sorry to disappoint… actually, you know what I’m not sorry at all,” Rio responds, as while she feels a lot of anger towards Jen, she also very much enjoys annoying her.

    “Of course you’re not,” Jen says, rolling her eyes. “What are you even doing here? Isn’t something like this beneath a cosmic being like you?” Jen asks, not being able to resist the opportunity to give Rio a hard time. “I’m here for my family,” Rio responds. “My wife, our children,” Rio says, stressing the ‘my wife’, just because she can.

    “Don’t you ever get sick of being so possessive?” Jen asks annoyed. “No, because of everything that has happened over the last year I have very right to be a little possessive,” Rio responds, the annoyance she is feeling towards Jen being perfectly clear in her voice.

    “Okay, that explains why you are being so possessive right now, but what was your excuse two hundred years ago?” Jen asks, looking annoyed, as in all the time she has known Rio she has known her to be incredibly possessive.

    “She’s my wife,” Rio responds, without hesitation, and Jen looks almost more annoyed.

    “Um, sorry,” a voice says and both Rio and Jen turn to see Prue standing outside the tent she shared with Nicky, Billy, and Tommy, it being perfectly clear that she heard at least some what Rio and Jen had said to each other. “I did not mean to interrupt,” Prue says, looking between the two of them. “It is okay, Sweet Girl,” Rio assures her daughter. “Are you okay? Did you sleep well?” Rio ask curious, and even Jen can see how completely different Rio is with her daughter than she as a few seconds earlier. “Yeah, I did,” Prue confirms. “Do you mind if I go for a bit of a walk?” Prue asks her mother curious, as she feels the need to get away from everyone.

    “Sure, just don’t go too far, don’t go down one of the paths to a trial,” Rio tells her daughter, knowing her well enough to know that she would considering trying to complete a task without everyone else if it meant protecting them, something which Rio wants to make sure to prevent from happening.

    “I won’t,” Prue promises her mother, before walking in the same direction that leads to the lake where Agatha went earlier, Rio watching her daughter as she goes.

    “Huh, you actually have a heart, who knew,” Jen says to Rio, who rolls her eyes, but can’t deny that Jen’s words hit a sore sport.

    “I am amazed you can recognize that, considering you don’t have a heart on your own,” Rio responds, lashing out due to what she is feeling. “Oh, I have a heart, you should ask Agatha just what my heart is like,” Jen says, with a smirk, as she cannot risk baiting Rio, even if she knows it is dangerous.

    “Why you…” Rio starts to say, but then she freezes as she feels something. “Get Agatha now!” Rio says, sounding terrified, before running in the direction Prue went in.

    Even though Jen is completely confused she knows Rio well enough to know that for her to sound so afraid, and for her to ask Jen of all people, to get Agatha then something must be horrifically wrong and because of that she listens.

    As she ran as fast as she could it only takes Rio a few moments to get to where Prue is, sitting on a rock, her knife in her hand, as blood flows out of her wrist.

    “Prue?” Rio asks, as she slowly approaches her daughter, doing her best to keep her voice calm even if she is feeling the furthest thing from it. “I forgot about the charm,” Prue admits, cursing herself for that, as Rio gets to her.

    “It’s okay,” Rio tells her daughter, who she realises hasn’t healed herself. “Prue? You are bleeding a lot, you need to heal yourself,” Rio tells her daughter, as she gets to her side, and sits on the rock next to Prue. “Soon,” Prue responds, looking down at her arm where the blood is dripping, as Agatha and Jen get to the clearing.

    “Keep the others away, including Nicky, Lilia will realise what is going on,” Agatha says to Jen, both of them having realised what Prue has done, something which fill them both with horror, and breaks Agatha’s heart. “I will,” Jen promises, feeling that that is the least she can do, as she walks back to the campsite while Agatha, who pushes down what she is feeling so that she can focus on Prue, walks over to her wife and daughter. “Prue, I don’t want to do anything against your will, but if you don’t heal yourself, I will heal you,” Rio tells her daughter, being able to tell that Prue is getting weaker, as Agatha gets to the two of them and kneels down on the road in front of them, while Rio will heal Prue herself if her daughter gets close to death she knows it would be important for Prue to make the choice to heal herself, to save herself.

    “Prue, sweetheart, look at me,” Agatha says in a gentle voice, trying to push down the horror she is feeling at the sight of how much her daughter is bleeding, and Prue looks at her. “Please Sweetheart, heal yourself. This is something you cannot take back, you don’t want to give up on life, not now,” Agatha tells her daughter. “Mom will heal you if you don’t heal yourself, because neither of us will never let you go, but Prue, I want you to choose this for yourself; you need to choose to survive, please,” Agatha begs her daughter, knowing that in a few seconds if Prue makes no effort to heal herself then Rio will intervene, but if that needs to happen then she knows that Prue is even further gone than she and Rio realised. “Okay,” Prue says, and she moves her other hand to cover the arm that is bleeding, and both Rio and Agatha watch purple magic come out of her hand and heal her arm, both Agatha and Rio being able to tell that she completely healed herself, something which fill them both with relief even if they know the physical wound will be much easier to heal than the emotional ones.

    “That’s good, Sweetheart,” Agatha tells her daughter, feeling that it is important to give her encouragement considering everything. “Prue, what happened Sweet Girl? In the past you’ve always healed yourself before it got to this,” Rio says to her daughter, clearly worried, as she knows just how bad the damage Prue did to herself was, and hearing that Agatha realises that whatever is going on with Prue, whatever drove her to hurt herself this time, is different from the other times she has done so. “I just keep thinking about how much I keep screwing up,” Prue admits. “How much I am hurting everyone,” Prue admits, pain and guilt in her voice.

    “What do you mean? You’re not hurting anyone,” Agatha says to her daughter, feeling very confused about what Prue is thinking about. “I am. I heard Mom and Jen fighting, it is hurting all three of you to be on this road together, Tommy was poisoned because of me, we are on the Road because of me, Infinity wants to hurt Nicky, Billy, and Tommy because of me… I broke everything,” Prue says, her voice breaking, the guilt she is feeling being perfectly clear in her voice, as while she would be fine with her choices having consequences on herself she feels guilty about the consequences her choices are having on everyone else.

    “Oh Prue, Sweetheart, it is not your fault,” Agatha assures her daughter, feeling her heart hurt because of how much pain she is in. “Jen and I have been fighting for over two hundred years, it is not your fault,” Rio tells her daughter. “Mama, Jen and I being on the Road is nothing we cannot handle, we’re all grownups, in fact, we all get some amusement out of fighting with each other,” Rio explains her daughter. “You do?” Prue asks, looking between her mothers, as she feels surprised by that.

    “We do,” Agatha assures her daughter. “Tommy chose to drink the wine, that wasn’t on you, he is capable of making his own choices, and is responsible for the consequences of those choices,” Agatha tells her daughter.

    “Just like the rest of us did when we choose to Walk the Road,” Rio tells her daughter. “Prue we all decided to walk the road, we all knew the risk,” Rio tells her.

    “But we consider it worth it because of what we will get at the end,” Agatha tells her daughter. “Yes, I am walking the road to save you, Nicky, Billy, and Tommy, but if you weren’t at risk I would still have considered it to get my magic back,” Agatha tells her daughter, feeling that it is important to show Prue that she isn’t the only person who is vulnerable, even if it goes against everything she is, as all she wants is for her daughter to be okay. “You do not have your magic?” Prue asks surprised, having no idea what that would feel like for her mother, as right now she cannot imagine what it would feel like not to have her magic, and she knows that her mother has had a lot longer than she has had.

    “No, Wanda took it,” Agatha tells her daughter. “And that makes me feel vulnerable, and guilty because I know it means that I can’t protect the people I love,” Agatha admits, and as Prue goes to say something Agatha realises exactly what her daughter is going to say. “No, you are not giving me your magic,” Agatha tells her daughter, there being no room for questioning in her voice. “Do not even try,” Agatha warns her daughter. “Yes Mama,” Prue responds, knowing that that is exactly what she was going to do, looking down at the ground, which causes Agatha and Rio to exchange looks.

    “Prue, you are not to blame for everything that has happened; it’s the fault of the stupid rules of the universe,” Agatha says, being able to feel the less than impressed look Rio is giving her at that. “I am so proud of you for breaking the spell on me, for helping Billy and Tommy, for standing up for Infinity, you have no reason to feel guilty, absolutely none,” Agatha assures her daughter, needing her to believe what she already believes. “Then why do I feel like this?” Prue asks, as she looks between her mothers.

    “Because emotions are impossible to explain, they are something we feel without reason,” Rio tells her daughter. “We experience them, they stay with us, but we cannot let them control us,” Rio tells her daughter. “What we can do is talk about them, share them,” Rio tells her daughter. “You do not have to carry the weight of anything you are feeling alone, you have us,” Rio tells her daughter.

    “Prue, you are not alone, you do not have to handle anything alone,” Agatha tells her daughter. “Letting your guilt consume you so much that you hurt yourself isn’t the answer, and isn’t what Mom and I want for you,” Agatha tells her daughter.

    “I do not know how to stop hurting myself,” Prue admits, feeling ashamed to admit that, as she thought she had more control than that. “We will help you figure out a way,” Rio promises her daughter. “We just need you to meet us in the middle and tell us when you are thinking of hurting yourself,” Agatha tells her. “Prue we will do whatever we can to help you, but we can’t do that if we don’t know you need help, so we need you to tell us when you are feeling the need to hurt yourself,” Agatha tells her daughter. “Do you think you can do that?” Agatha asks curious.

    “I… I think so,” Prue responds, and in response Agatha, and Rio both hug their daughter, both wanting to do everything they can to show her that she is not alone, both feeling terrified about the real possibility of loosing her. A little while after she left Agatha, Rio, and Prue Jen is sitting in the campsite, having been joined by Lilia, Nicky, Billy, Tommy, Sharon and Alice. To all of their surprise a small amount of food has appeared in the campsite.

    “Do you think it’s safe to eat this?” Tommy asks curious, as everyone hesitantly inspects the food.

    “We are not in a trial,” Sharon points out.

    “Doesn’t necessarily mean it is safe to eat,” Lilia tells her. “I feel like it would be,” Nicky admits. “It is like the campsite, given to use to help us while here,” Nicky admits.

    “Is that a prediction?” Billy asks curious, as he knows that will tell them a lot.

    “Um… I am not sure, I think so,” Nicky admits. “Where are Mom, Mama and Prue?” Nicky asks, looking at Jen, knowing she was the first one awake.

    “They went for a walk, I am sure they will be back soon,” Jen says, trying to say as little as possible, though from the look on Lilia’s face it is clear she realises something more is going on, but it is just as clear that Lilia knows better than talking about something like that in front of the whole group.

    “So, do we eat the food or not?” Tommy asks, looking between the others. “I am,” Nicky says, before picking up one of the sandwiches that has appeared. “I trust what I feel,” Nicky says.

    “Nicky no!” Jen objects, not wanting something to happen to him, but Nicky ignores her and takes a bite of the sandwich.

    “How do you feel?” Lilia asks concerned, once Nicky has had a chance to swallow the bite he has taken.

    “Fine, it is delicious,” Nicky admits. “I think we are okay,” Nicky tells the others.

    “Good enough for me,” Tommy says, before picking up a sandwich of his own, and trusting his brother Billy does the same.

    “The second anyone feels like something is wrong, say it,” Jen says, as she, Sharon, Lilia and Alice all also pick up some food.

    For the next few minutes, the group eat the food that eat the food that appeared, and it quickly becomes clear that there is absolutely nothing wrong with the food, and actually it is quite delicious.

    “Do you think I should take food to Mom, Mama, and Prue?” Nicky asks, clearly worried about his family, looking between the others and because of that he doesn’t realise that his mothers, and sister are rejoining them. “No need, Sweetheart, we’re here,” Rio says as the trio walk into the campsite, Jen realising that the three of them must have used the lake to wash the blood of Prue.

    “So, we’re just eating food that has randomly appeared now?” Agatha asks, as she looks between the others. “Didn’t we learn anything?” Agatha asks, feeling that that was a very bad idea.

    “It is safe, Mama, I knew it,” Nicky assures her.

    “That’s good enough for me,” Rio says, trusting her son, as she, Prue and Agatha all sit down.

    Once the trio sit down Nicky hands each of them some of the food that he has been keeping safe for them as he wanted to make sure that he saved them some food.

    “Thank you,” Prue says to her brother, as she takes the food and starts to eat.

    “So, three trials to go,” Alice comments. “Should we talk about which trial to do next?” Alice asks, feeling that that is a good place to start, preferably between Jen, Agatha and Rio start fighting again.

    “Probably,” Jen admits. “We’ve got Agatha and Billy’s trial, yours and Prue’s, and Lilia’s and Tommy’s to go,” Jen says, knowing that she doesn’t want them to do Prue’s trial next as after what she just witnessed, she doesn’t want the young girl to be stressed more than she already is. “Which one do we do?” Jen asks, as she looks between the others, knowing that this is a decision they need to make together.

    “I am happy to do mine,” Billy says.

    “Same,” Tommy confirms.

    “I think we should do mine,” Lilia says, like Jen she doesn’t want Prue to have the added stress of her trial right now, and she is sure that Agatha’s trial will have the potential to cause all Agatha, Rio, and all four of the kids’ pain so she wants to avoid that as long as possible.

    “Zietta, are you sure?” Agatha asks her curious, wanting to make sure she is okay with that, but she is also grateful that Lilia has volunteered. “Yeah, I am,” Lilia responds, and from the look on her aunts face Agatha knows that she is completely serious.

    “Okay,” Agatha says with a nod. “Tommy, is that okay with you?” Agatha asks him, as she knows it is his trial too.

    “Yep, fine with me,” Tommy responds.

    “Okay, we’ll finish eating and then do down the yellow brick, or in this case leaf, road,” Rio responds.

    “How do you even know about the Wizard of Oz?” Jen asks surprised. “The Wicked Witch of the East is based on me,” Agatha reveals. “Really?” Billy and Tommy ask excited, while Prue and Nicky exchange confused look, neither of them understanding what the big deal about that is, and Jen rolls her eyes.

    “Really,” Agatha confirms. “I’ll tell you the story later,” Agatha tells the boys.

    “That would be amazing,” Tommy says amazed, very much looking forward to that.

    “So, we are in agreement, we will do the Lilia and Tommy’s trial next?” Sharon asks, looking around, and everyone nods. “Then let’s finish eating,” Sharon says, and everyone does just that.

    About ten minutes later everyone has finished eating and the entire coven are walking down the yellow path together, it being perfectly clear that they are all feeling extremely nervous about what they are going to find. “Wow,” Nicky says amazed, as they approach what looks to be a castle. “That’s different,” Billy says amazed.

    “Really is,” Tommy confirms.

    “Are you ready, Zietta?” Prue asks her aunt curious.

    “Yes, I am,” Lilia responds. “Tommy, are you?” Lilia asks him concerned. “Yes, I am,” Tommy responds.

    “Then in we go,” Alice says, trying to hide how concerned she is, and the ten of them heading into the second trial, all feeling very nervous about what they are going to find, while Agatha and Rio are also feeling extremely concerned about their daughter and how she is going to handle completing a trial after everything that has happened.

    Chapter 56

    Chapter 56 AN: Um, so I just finished writing the last chapter of this story. I didn’t intend for it to be finished so soon, but I feel like it came to its logical conclusion. I hope you’re okay with the decision I have made, and where I have decided to end the story.

    I know nothing about Tarot, everything I have included in this chapter is based on research I have done, I apologize in advance if I am completely wrong. I did enjoy working out the tarot for everyone, so I hope you like that too.

    As everyone walks into the trial there is a flash of white light and as it fades away it becomes clear to Lilia and Tommy, both of whom are wearing the kind of clothes that Lilia wore when she was a child, that they are alone. As well as being along Lilia and Tommy see that they are standing on a small, what seems like floating, platform, that is connected to another, what seems to be, larger floating stone platform by, what looks to be, a very unsteady bridge.

    “Where are the others?” Tommy asks worried, terrified for his bother, as he knows that after everything that has happened he cannot loose his brother, that that is the one thing he cannot handle.

    “I suspect that our trial will lead to us being re-united with them,” Lilia explains.

    “Makes sense,” Tommy realises. “Do you think the bridge will be able to hold us?” Tommy asks, feeling concerned, as the bridge doesn’t seem very stable.

    “I don’t know,” Lilia admits, feeling uncertain, as while it seems like the obvious option it doesn’t seem like the safest.

    “Should I run us over?” Tommy asks, thinking that it could be a good idea. “That is probably the best idea,” Lilia admits, as she knows that the trial will use both of their abilities so it would make sense if Tommy had to use his speed.

    “Okay,” Tommy says, and he takes Lilia’s hand and superspeed them over the bridge, getting to the large platform that is middle just as the bridge falls below. “Okay that worked,” Tommy says, as he and Lilia, who is struggling to keep her composure, realise that most of the platform is taken up by a very large table.

    Exchanging looks Lilia and Tommy walk over to the very large, clearly very old, table and on the table they realise there is a large stack of tarot cards, an large hour glass, and Infront of the timer is a single spot for a tarot card. Looking around the rest of the table Tommy and Lilia realises that around the edge of the table, carved into the stone, is the name of each member of the coven with space for five cards in front of it. “Do we have to match the tarot card to the person?” Tommy asks, feeling that that would make sense, but he doesn’t know a lot about tarot so he cannot be certain.

    “Yes, one card from each of the five categories of cards for each person,” Lilia reveals, everything making perfect sense to her.

    “Okay, that would be your part, what do you think mine is?” Tommy asks, as from the way the trial works, he knows he would have to have his own part.

    “I suspect that you will be reasonable for getting our people back here,” Lilia says as she picks up the cards and starts to shuffle, feeling that that is the most likely option.

    “Makes sense,” Tommy realises, as Lilia draws the first card. “Three of pentacles,” Lilia reads. “Collaboration, community, singular voices waiting to harmonize,” Lilia says.

    “Sounds like us, the coven,” Tommy realises, as even though he is not technically a witch he does feel like he is apart of the coven. “Yes, it does,” Lilia confirms before placing the card in the singular spot in front of the timer, the spot she realises represents the coven, as soon as she puts it down the timer starts.

    “So do you just draw cards and put them where they fit?” Tommy asks curious, trying to make sense of exactly what this trial is. “No, I pick a person and complete their spread,” Lilia explains, knowing she will use a card drawn after completing one person’s spread to tell her who to do next. “We will save you and I for last,” Lilia says, feeling that that is best, and Tommy nods in agreement.

    “Then who do we start with?” Tommy asks.

    “Agatha,” Lilia says, just knowing that, and she walks over to where Agatha’s name is, shuffling the cards as she goes, and once she gets to Agatha’s name, she pulls the first card. “The Hierophant, but reversed, that means rebellion, subversiveness, new approaches as desire to go ahead and regain control as well as to break free from the shackles of convention,” Lilia recites, “Temptation to try unorthodox approaches or to function in a way which defies social ties and norms,” Lilia says.

    “That sounds a lot like Agatha,” Tommy realises.

    “Really does,” Lilia confirms as she draws the next card. “King of wands, natural board leader, extremely capable, takes control,” Lilia sys as she places the card.

    “Agatha’s a leader?” Tommy asks surprised, as while the rest of it sounds like Agatha, he isn’t overly sure that that sounds like her. “Yes, she shies away from it, but she is a natural leader, she is just afraid to embrace that part of herself,” Lilia explains, knowing Agatha well enough to know that, as she draws the next card. “Five of cups, dwelling in the past, inducing feelings of self-pity and regret, incapable of moving on, or learning from mistakes,” Lilia says, knowing that is fitting considering what happened to the twins and Evanora, but because she doesn’t want Tommy to ask about that, as it is not her place to explain, she quickly draws the next card. “Three of swords, Heartbreak, sorrow, grief,” Lilia says, putting it down, her heart hurting for Agatha as she does so, but knowing that it describes her perfectly.

    “That really isn’t a happy card,” Tommy realises, frowning, as he feels bad for Agatha.

    “It is not,” Lilia says as she places the next card, the last card for Agatha. “Five of pentacles, hardship, loss, isolation, feeling abandoned,” Lilia says, guilt in her voice, as she knows that Agatha felt abandoned because of her, because she wasn’t there for Agatha when she needed her the most. “That really isn’t a happy spread,” Tommy realises, frowning as he feels bad about someone he cares about.

Are you okay?” Agatha asks her son concerned.

    “I know,” Agatha says, before leaning up and kissing Rio, puling her in closer as she does, as right now, after everything that has happened, all she needs is her wife.

    “I don’t know,” Alice admits. “She would have loved this,” Alice admits. “Your mom?” Jen asks, as that is what she assumes, and Alice nods. “She always said the Road would save me,” Alice admits. “When I was really little, we would talk about coming her together, completing it together,” Alice says as she stares at a picture of what looks like a women singing surrounded by fire.

    “Me too,” Alice responds.

    “Lilia?” Sharon asks concerned, and as Lilia turns to look at her Sharon sees that she has tears in her eyes. “You knew someone who was burned at the stake,” Sharon realises, knowing that that happened during the Witch Trials of the old days, but at the same time it is shocking that Lilia has experienced that.

    “Yes,” Lilia says, trying to fight back her tears, as she remembers what it was like, what she felt like.

    “I’m so sorry,” Sharon says before hugging her, offering her comfort, having no idea what else to say.

    Across the room from where Sharon and Lilia are, as Tommy zooms around the entire room, Billy and Nicky are searching for the item that will start the trial.

    “All these papers have details on them,” Billy says amazed. “Look, there is even a paper that has real articles,” Billy says, showing Nicky what he has found.

    “That is incredible,” Nicky says, sounding amazed, as he takes the newspaper so that he can have a better look. “Everything The Road has created is so detailed,” Nicky says.

    “Really is,” Billy admits. “It reminds me of what my mom created with her magic,” Billy admits, not even realising that he called Wanda mom. “Do you think the Road was created by chaos magic?” Nicky asks curious, though he has to assume that if the Road was created by Chaos magic then, at least, Prue would have been able to tell that.

    “No,” Billy says, shaking his head. “The Road feels more… grounded, does that make sense?” Billy asks, sounding uncertain, as while that makes sense to him, he isn’t sure if it will make sense to anyone else. “Strangely enough, it does,” Nicky admits. “But it is interesting that there are similarities,” Nicky admits, trying to figure out what that means. “Really is,” Billy responds, and the two of them continue to search for the item that will start the final trial.

    Searching the middle of the room for a way to start the trial, feeling nervous but determined, Prue, like her brothers, is searching for what will start the trial and as she searches, she hears a woosh that tells her Tommy is using his powers, and he appears next to her.

    “It’s not just Prue’s trial,” Jen says, looking at Alice, who is inspecting the record. “Alice?” Jen asks, noticing the look on her face.

    “What do you know?” Rio asks, ask, looking at her, but Alice seems to be frozen, as Prue continues to fight the ‘creature’. “ALICE!” Rio exclaims, feeling terrified for her daughter.

    “I didn’t think it was real,” Alice says, sounding horrified. “Didn’t think what was real?” Sharon asks her in a gentle voice. “I thought it was just me, that it’s my fault that I can’t keep a job, that everything I touch turn to shut, that I couldn’t save her,” Alice says, guilt in her voice, as tears come to her eyes. “I convinced myself they were birthmarks, even though she had the same ones,” Alice says, as she lowers her shirt to show the same burns on the shoulders that can now be seen on Lilia.

    “Wait, are we talking about a generational curse?” Jen asks shocked. “Oh, you poor thing,” Lilia says, to her, sounding sympathetic. “Poor us! Now we have her family’s old-ass curse!” Jen exclaims, looking horrified, as she knows how bad that is.

    “Great! We know what it is! Can we please move on to how to destroy it!” Prue requests. “My blasts are holding it at bay, but it is not hurting it!” Prue exclaims, sending more blasts of purple magic, to the others it looks like she is blasting nothing, but Prue knows is actually doing her best to hold the representation of the curse at bay, and as she looks towards her daughter Agatha realises something.

    “Prue, you’re hurt,” Agatha says, looking worriedly at her daughter, who has a few burns, and cuts, on her arms and torso.

    “I know. I will heal myself when the curse is destroyed,” Prue says, not feeling concerned. “But I would really appreciate it if you could hurry up and figure out how to destroy it,” Prue says, as she sends a stronger blast of magic towards the curse, and while it does seem to knock the curse a little, it doesn’t cause damage.

    “We need a plan!” Rio realises, feeling worried about her daughter, as she glances towards Agatha, who is watching Alice and realises something. “You’re right, that’s the solution,” Agatha says to Alice, who is glancing at the piano.

    “No, it’s not,” Alice says, really not wanting to do what she realises Agatha is thinking.

    “What?” Nicky asks, looking between his mama and where his sister is fighting something, what appears to be, invisible, not being able to help but feel incredibly concerned about her.

    “We have to play Lorna’s Ballard,” Agatha reveals.

    “I’m not playing that song!” Alice objects as she really doesn’t want to do that.

    “I think you have to,” Prue says, as she winches as she fails to prevent a blast of fire from hitting her.

    “Prue’s right, all signs point to a jam session,” Agatha tells Alice, feeling terrified for her daughter.

    “What good will it do? The ballad opens the Road, we did that, we’re here, we’re almost at the end,” Alice points out.

    “Lorna’s version is very different to what I wrote, I have been listening to it a lot,” Nicky says, knowing that.

    “Which means we need to figure out what Lorna wanted form the Road? What was her intention?” Agatha asks, trying to figure out the answer. “To save her daughter,” Rio, who has sat down at the drum set, says, glancing over at Prue, feeling the worry she is feeling towards her daughter grow.

    “You should have brunt to a crisp years ago, but here you are,” Agatha says to Alice. “Sullen and aimless, but alive, that’s because at any given moment somewhere, someone, is playing that song you hate so much,” Agatha realises. “Lorna’s ballad is a protection spell, it protected you,” Agatha says, pointing to her. “And maybe now it can protect us,” Agatha says, looking at her daughter, knowing that what she wants most right now is to protect her daughter.

    “Sounds like a really good plan to me, this thing is getting more determined,” Prue reveals.

    “Can you keep fighting it?” Nicky asks his sister, sounding worried. “I have to, but the rest of you have to perform the song,” Prue tells them. “Alice, piano?” Agatha asks, and she nods. “Zietta, can you play anything?” Agatha asks, assuming that Rio is going to play the drums because that is where she is sitting.

    “Zills,” Lilia answers.

    “Not sure how much help that is going to be,” Agatha mutters. “Does anyone play guitar?” Agatha asks.

    “A little,” Billy says, hurrying over to get one.

    “Tommy? Sharon? Jen?” Agatha asks, looking between them, knowing that Nicky is going to be singing with her.

    “Bongoes,” Sharon says, hurrying over to where they are.

    “I’ll give the base a try,” Jen say, hurrying over to that. “There’s a keytar, I’ve always wanted to try that,” Tommy says, walking over to where that is.

    “Play it right, play it well, and maybe we won’t die,” Agatha tells the others, and as Prue continues to fight the physical manifestation of Alice’s curse the others start to play; “I have learned the lesson Of all that's foul and fair Our love was forged in fire Water, earth, and air The spell is cast, how long it lasts I cannot divine The road is there And so I dare To risk this heart of mine”, Agatha and Nicky say, and as they reach the chorus the others, with the exception of Prue who is too preoccupied with fighting the manifestation of the curse, join in and continue to sing the Ballard together. Over the next couple of minutes everyone sings, and plays, and as they get closer to finishing the spell everyone, not just Prue, can see the representation of the curse, and as she actually sees it Alice starts to play harder, doing her best to do what her mother always wanted her to, and finish the song.

    “We did it,” Alice says amazed, as the physical representation of the spell is destroyed, and the piano opens, clearly the way to exit the final trial. “Yeah, we did,” Billy says amazed, as Agatha and Rio hurry over to their daughter, while the others hug Alice, who is clearly feeling overwhelmingly happy.

    “Are you okay?” Rio asks her daughter worried, both her and Agatha resisting the urge to hug their daughter as they know that with her burns they would risk making them worse.

    “I think so,” Prue admits. “I am going to need some time to heal all my injures,” Prue realises.

    “Start with your torso, they are the most server,” Agatha tells her daughter, being able to tell that.

    “Okay,” Prue says, and she does what her mother suggested and heals her most severe injury.

    “Good, do you think you can make your way out of the trial?” Rio asks her daughter, once she has heard her injury, knowing that that will give her a bit more of an insight into how hurt Prue actually is.

    “In a moment,” Prue says, reaching down and healing her calf as she has a pretty big burn there. “That is better,” Prue realises.

    “Are you in much pain?” Agatha asks worried.

    “Not a lot,” Prue assures her mother. “I will be fine,” Prue assures her mothers. “We should get out of here,” Prue tells her mothers. “Yeah, we should,” Agatha confirms, as the others walk over to her, Rio, and Prue.

    “Is this it? have we completed the road?” Tommy asks.

    “Looks like it,” Lilia confirms.

    “So, what are we going to find when we leave this task?” Billy asks curious.

    “That is a very, very good question,” Jen admits.

    “How do you feel?” Prue asks, looking at Alice.

    “Free,” Alice admits, feeling amazed. “How about you?” Alice asks curious.

    “Proud,” Prue responds. “And sore,” Prue admits.

    “Then we should get out of here so you can look after yourself,” Nicky tells his sister, clearly worried about her.

    “Probably a good idea,” Prue responds, and once she does, they all head over to the piano and head out of the trial, Prue, needing to be helped out by her mothers as she is clearly feeling some pain.

    As everyone exits the trial, they find that they are once again back at the campsite, but unlike every other time they have come out of a trial the campsite is not empty as there is someone waiting for them, an incredibly powerful, woman.

    “Hecate?” Rio asks surprised, having not expected to see her. “The goddess of magic?” Agatha says, looking at her with an amazed look on her face as she reaches up and puts her hand on her locket, not being able to believe that they are within the presence of the Goddess of magic herself.

Once again, thank you for all the support you have given me.

    “You are the goddess of magic?” Prue asks amazed, being able to ‘feel’ the power that the being Infront of them is radiating, and she can’t help but feel comforted by that, it feels familiar, like it is something she has always known.

    “Yes, I am,” Hecate confirms.

    “Wow, it is an honor to meet you,” Prue says amazed.

    “I am very amazed to finally meet you too, Prudence,” Hecate says, giving Prue a look that Prue can’t describe, but which makes her feel seen, makes her feel safe.

    “To talk to you, my coven,” Hecate says, as she looks between the group. “Please, sit down,” Hecate says, gesturing to the different places to sit that are around the fire.

    “No, my child,” Hecate assures him. “Sit, sit,” Hecate says, as she sits down, and everyone looks at Rio who they know has the most experience with cosmic beings, and she nods, not being able to explain why, but she knows that Hecate won’t hurt them. After seeing Rio nod everyone sits down, feeling very confused about what is going on. “I have been waiting a long time to meet you all,” Hecate says as she looks between the members of the coven.

    “You have?” Alice asks surprised, as she certainly wasn’t expecting that. “Yes,” Hecate confirms. “I long ago knew that there would one day be the right coven, at the right time, brought together by fate, by the need you all share. I knew that together you would be capable of the impossible,” Hecate explains.

    “What is the need we all share?” Jen asks, feeling interested, but also a little concerned about what Hecate could be talking about.

    “The need to be apart of something, to be supported, to not be as alone as you have been made to feel,” Hecate explains, the sorrow she feels towards the members of the group being perfectly clear in her voice as she says that. “Sounds about right,” Agatha mutters.

    “What was with the trials? if you knew about us a long time ago, if you knew we were the right coven, why did you make us do the trials?” Rio asks, an angry edge to her voice, as it seemed excessive, seems like she just put them through pain, put her family in danger, for no reason. “Because you needed to see what I knew,” Hacete says. “You needed to become what I knew you could be, you needed to bond,” Hecate explains, as she looks between the members of the coven.

    “So you made us undertake trials to prove that we were the ‘right coven’,” Jen realizes, frowning, as like Agatha, she isn’t’ sure how to feel about that. “Yes, but more important you needed to see just what you are capable of, you needed to believe what I already knew, that you need each other,” Hecate explains.

    “I knew that wasn’t going to happen,” Hacete explains. “You have all been forged in fire, all of you have had your own battles, have your own scars,” Hecate admits. “Every single one of you likes to believe that you don’t need anyone, but you do, you needed to believe that it needed to be proved to you,” Hecate explains.

    “You couldn’t have just told us that we needed each other?” Agatha asks, that seems like the more logical solution to her.

    “None of you would have listened,” Hecate responds.

Feeling very curious, and a little nervous about what is going to happen, Rio, after exchanging looks with Agatha, stands up and walks over to Hecate. “You can ask your question,” Hecate says to her.

    “Yes, you know the truth of what happened to your mother, that is an incredible gift, but I still have another one for you,” Hecate says, making an amulet, what looks like a necklace, appear in her hand. “You are a protection witch, this amulet will allow you to detect when a witch has been cursed like you were, it will allow you to protect others in the way you wish you were able to protect your mother,” Hecate says, handing Alice the amulet.

Childhood, and everything that comes along with it, it is the one thing not even the four of you can get back,” Hecate tells them. “Rio, Lilia, Agatha, Sharon, Jennifer, Alice, you are all now apart of a coven, a family, embrace that, do not run from it, do not run from each other,” Hecate says, before disappearing.
